The importance of free software to science
[LWN subscriber-only content]
June 4, 2025
This article was contributed by Lee Phillips
Free software plays a critical role in science, both in research and in
disseminating it. Aspects of software freedom are directly relevant to
simulation, analysis, document preparation and preservation, security,
reproducibility, and usability. Free software brings practical and specific
advantages, beyond just its ideological roots, to science, while
proprietary software comes with equally specific risks.  As a practicing
scientist, I would like to help others—scientists or not—see the benefits
from free software in science.
Although there is an implicit philosophical stance here—that
reproducibility and openness in science are desirable, for instance—it is
simply a fact that a working scientist will use the best tools for the job,
even if those might not strictly conform to the laudable goals of the
free-software movement. It turns out that free software, by virtue of its
freedom, is often the best tool for the job.
Reproducing results
Scientific progress depends, at its core, on
reproducibility
. Traditionally, this referred to the results of
experiments: it should be possible to attempt their replication by
following the procedures described in papers. In the case of a failure to
replicate the results, there should be enough information in the paper to
make that
finding meaningful.

1 month trial subscription
The use of computers in science adds some extra dimensions to this
concept. If the conclusions depend on some complex data massaging using a
computer program, another researcher should be able to run the same program
on the original or new data. Simulations should be reproducible by running
the identical simulation code. In both cases this implies access to, and the
right to distribute, the relevant source code. A mere description of the
algorithms used, or a mention of the name of a commercial software product,
is not good enough to satisfy the demands of a meaningful attempt at
replication.
The source code alone is sometimes not enough. Since the details of the
results of a calculation can depend on the compiler, the entire chain from
source to machine code needs to be free to ensure reproducibility. This
condition is automatically met for languages like
Julia
,
Python
, and
R
, whose interpreters and
compilers are free software. For C, C++, and Fortran, the other currently
popular languages for simulation and analysis, this is only sometimes the
case. To get the best performance from Fortran simulations, for example,
scientists often use commercial compilers provided by chip manufacturers.
Document preparation and
preservation
The forward march of science is recorded in papers which are collected on
preprint servers (such as
arXiv
), on the home pages of
scientists, and published in journals. It's obviously bad for science if
future generations can't read these papers, or if a researcher can no
longer open a manuscript after upgrading their word-processing
software. Fortunately, the
future readability of published papers is enabled by the adoption, by
journals and preprint servers, of PDF as the universal standard format for
the distribution of published work. This has been the case even with journals
that request Microsoft Word files for manuscript submission.
PDF files are based on an open, versioned standard and will be readable
into the foreseeable future with all of the formatting details
preserved. This is essential in science, where communication is not merely
through words but depends on figures, captions, typography, tables, and
equations. Outside the world of scientific papers, HTML is by far the
dominant markup language used for online communication. It has advantages
over PDF in that simple documents take less bandwidth, HTML is more easily
machine-readable and human-editable, and by default text flows to fit the
reader's viewport. But this last advantage is an example of why HTML is not
ideal for scientific communication: its flexibility means that documents
can appear differently on different devices.
The final rendering of a web document is the result of interpretation of
HTML and CSS by the browser. The display of mathematics typically depends
on evolving JavaScript libraries, as well, so the author does not know
whether the reader is seeing what was intended. The "P" in PDF stands for
"portable": every reader sees the same thing, on every device, using the
same fonts, which should be embedded into the file. The archival demands
of the scientific record, combined with the typographic complexity of

data.title: Mistral Code
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Mistral Code是一款企业级AI编码助手，提供智能代码补全、生成和自主任务执行功能。它利用先进的人工智能模型，如Codestral和Devstral，能够深度理解代码库，并在开发者工作的IDE中直接运行。其特点包括上下文感知的代码理解、自主编码、实时代码补全、代码编辑和智能搜索等。Mistral Code帮助开发团队提高生产力，支持代码调试、重构、文档生成、测试、迁移和性能优化。该工具可定制并确保代码隐私和安全，适合在重要代码环境中部署，提供一体化平台和快速支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mistral Code Enterprise的产品定位、定价模式及其市场反应

不同观点：
• **对企业销售模式的支持**：一些评论认为，Mistral Code的"联系我们"定价和企业级销售模式是合理的，尤其是针对那些出于安全或其他原因无法使用前沿模型的组织。这类客户通常需要经过企业销售流程、安全审查等，因此这种模式对他们而言并不构成重大障碍（如mwigdahl的观点）。

• **对产品质量和市场竞争力的质疑**：一些评论质疑Mistral模型的质量和市场竞争力，认为如果Mistral拥有领先的模型，他们会提供透明的定价。还有人将Mistral与现有的免费工具（如Aider、Claude Code等）进行比较，质疑其独特价值（如tormeh和joshstrange的观点）。

• **对定价和市场策略的不满**：有评论指出，Mistral不仅要求用户联系销售团队获取定价，还要求提供公司规模和收入等信息，这种做法被认为是不合理的，尤其是对于想要支持欧洲AI公司的欧洲企业来说（如coolgoose的观点）。

补充讨论：
• **产品信息不明确**：一些评论提到Mistral的官网信息不清晰，用户难以找到产品的基本信息，如产品类型和功能描述（如kiratp的观点）。

• **市场需求和时机**：有评论讨论了为何现在突然出现这么多代码助手应用，并猜测这可能与LLM性能的 plateau 有关，市场竞争从模型性能转向应用功能（如abdullahkhalids的观点）。

• **技术实现和替代方案**：一些评论提到了现有的免费替代方案，如使用zed + ollama实现类似的功能，或者使用Aider等工具作为Mistral的后端（如mirekrusin和KolmogorovComp的观点）。

争议焦点：
• **企业销售模式的合理性**：一方认为这种模式适合企业客户，另一方则认为不让个人开发者试用会导致负面市场反应。
• **产品的市场竞争力**：一方质疑Mistral的模型质量和定价策略，另一方则提到市场上已有免费替代方案。

data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 本文是一则验证请求通知，Radware Bot Manager要求用户通过勾选框来确认自己是人类，以确保网站安全。若无法完成验证，用户可以通过提供的链接联系支持团队，并附上问题截图。同时附有事件ID以供参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oort云中的螺旋结构及其发现的意义

不同观点：
• doctoboggan指出，螺旋结构是通过在Hayden Planetarium的模拟中首次发现的，这一发现是通过为一个描述和可视化Oort云的新太空展览做准备时获得的，并附上了模拟动画的链接。
• coke12认为，这一发现非常酷，并指出我们自己的太阳系似乎也有螺旋臂。
• dedicate表示，他们以前想象Oort云像是一场发生在偏远地区的散乱的雪球战斗，并质疑如此精致的结构如何在那样遥远的地方保持形状，认为这一发现彻底改变了对太阳系“边缘”的看法。
• Eduard请求解释这一发现的 significance（意义），询问这是否是因为在一个以前被认为随机分布的区域中发现了可定义的结构。
• machenesonk提出了一个更广泛的问题，询问宇宙是否可以自转。
• girvo提到了技术问题，表示无法进入网站，因为hCaptcha中的图像（桌子和椅子）从未加载出来，即使点击了20多次“跳过”。
• HappMacDonald以一种幽默的方式评论，提到Kamina可能会赞同这一发现，但没有深入讨论科学内容。

补充讨论：
• 关于Oort云螺旋结构的发现，讨论的焦点在于这一结构的独特性和其对理解太阳系边缘的意义。
• Eduard的问题引发了对发现科学意义的深入探讨，特别是对以前认为随机分布区域的新认识。
• machenesonk的问题虽然偏离主题，但引发了关于宇宙整体结构和运动的思考。
• girvo的技术问题虽然与主要讨论点无关，但提示了访问和参与讨论的潜在障碍。

data.title: After court order, OpenAI is now preserving all ChatGPT user logs
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 因法院命令需保留所有输出日志数据，引发的隐私、法律和商业影响讨论。

不同观点：
• **[lxgr]**: 指出欧洲法院和政府不会乐见其法律和意见被无视，尤其是隐私法规被加引号处理。这意味着OpenAI可能违反了多项隐私法规。
• **[efskap]**: 强调这一命令不仅影响ChatGPT用户，还影响使用OpenAI API的用户，包括免费版、Plus版和Pro版的用户，可能对OpenAI的业务造成负面影响。
• **[paxys]**: 提出OpenAI不仅需要保留这些数据，还可能被要求在法律诉讼中分享数据，这可能导致用户隐私泄露，甚至在法庭上公开私人对话。
• **[celnardur]**: 认为LLM（大语言模型）的隐私问题一直是其致命弱点，特别是在处理敏感工作数据时，如代码和受监管数据，无法信任云端工具，直到这些工具可以本地化运行。
• **[ronsor]**: 强调法院命令可能违反多个司法管辖区的隐私法和OpenAI与客户的现有合同。
• **[solfox]**: 指出其他AI系统（如Google Gemini、Grok等）也可能面临类似命令，建议使用替代工具避免隐私问题。
• **[Imnimo]**: 质疑OpenAI是否会通知用户其数据保留政策的变化，还是让企业通过媒体得知，这可能影响企业的信任和使用决策。
• **[DevX101]**: 提到一些企业因不信任OpenAI的数据处理方式而选择自托管LLM模型，这一事件证明了他们的决定是正确的。

补充讨论：
• **链接和访问问题**: 多个评论者提供了相关文章链接，并讨论了由于流量过大导致链接无法访问的问题，部分用户通过存档网站（如Wayback Machine）访问内容。
• **法律和隐私责任**: 一些用户（如[jwpapi]）对现有API使用的法律和隐私责任表示困惑，特别是当通过API密钥使用OpenAI服务时，责任归属问题。
• **数据所有权和透明度**: [MeIam] 质疑《纽约时报》等实体是否有权查看用户数据，反映了对数据所有权和透明度的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 法院命令与隐私法规的冲突：OpenAI是否应该遵守法院命令，即使这可能违反隐私法和用户协议。
• 数据保留和用户隐私：OpenAI保留所有日志数据是否会严重影响用户隐私，尤其是在法律诉讼中可能被要求披露这些数据。
• 对业务的影响：这一命令对OpenAI及其客户，特别是依赖API的企业用户，可能带来的商业和法律风险。

data.author: kklisura

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的自动驾驶技术、数据记录、以及相关的法律和透明度问题。

不同观点：
• [批评特斯拉和监管不足]：isodev认为特斯拉在车祸判定上的延迟是不合理的，特别是等待安全气囊展开才记录为车祸，显示出监管的缺失。他们表示不理解为什么还有人会选择购买特斯拉。

• [数据公开的必要性]：duxup认为，如果国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）拥有数据，那么纳税人也应有权访问这些数据，除非有非常合理的理由不公开。

• [实际事故案例]：mosdl分享了一个亲属涉及特斯拉自动驾驶车祸的案例，目前尚不清楚谁的责任，但初步报告显示事故发生时特斯拉处于自动驾驶模式，情况对特斯拉不利。

• [技术与法规分析]：dhx详细解释了联合国和美国的法规对车辆事件数据记录（EDR）的要求，指出这些法规并没有涵盖自动驾驶系统（ADS/ADAS）的操作数据。目前，特斯拉自愿记录的某些数据可能包括ADS/ADAS操作信息，但这不是法规要求的。

• [媒体与利益冲突]：jfoster指出，这起案件由《华盛顿邮报》报道，而该报的拥有者同时也是自动驾驶公司Zoox的拥有者，暗示可能存在利益冲突。

• [更多事故案例]：1vuio0pswjnm7提供了多个NTSB调查链接，展示特斯拉涉及的事故案例，包括电池起火事故。

• [支持特斯拉的自动驾驶体验]：cowlby以个人经验支持特斯拉的自动驾驶功能，认为硬件和软件的升级带来了显著的驾驶体验改善，并认为这是值得每月$99的安全功能。

• [对透明度的讽刺]：kergonath简短地讽刺了特斯拉的透明度问题。

• [对特斯拉法律纠纷的不满]：londons_explore作为股东，对特斯拉将资金投入法律纠纷而不是产品开发表示不满，认为 crash报告中的软件版本号等信息不重要。

• [对自动驾驶监管的期待]：JumpCrisscross期待加拿大、欧盟或加州等地提高对仅依靠摄像头自动驾驶汽车的审批标准，甚至可能实施禁令。

• [对特斯拉领导层和销售的批评]：xyst批评特斯拉的领导层，并希望其全球销售继续下降。

• [公众数据需求]：7e认为公共道路上的数据应公开，公众有权知道周围特斯拉车辆带来的风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于特斯拉自动驾驶技术的安全性和数据透明度，以及现有法规是否足够保护公众利益。
• 不同用户对特斯拉的看法两极化，有人批评其技术不成熟和法律纠纷，也有人支持其自动驾驶功能并认为体验良好。
• 媒体在报道此类事件中的角色和可能的利益冲突也被提及。

data.title: Not all tokens are meant to be forgotten
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种针对性信息遗忘（TIF）框架，以解决大型语言模型（LLM）在遗忘不必要信息时的“过度遗忘”问题。TIF框架通过识别遗忘样本中的 unwanted words (UW) 和 general words (GW)，利用逻辑偏好损失函数来遗忘UW相关信息，同时通过保留损失函数保护GW中的有用信息，从而提高遗忘效果并减少模型效用损失。实验表明，TIF在TOFU和MUSE基准上取得了显著效果，有效提升了遗忘效率并保持了模型实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语言模型在记忆和遗忘信息方面的能力及其影响

不同观点：
• JimDabell认为，根据Meta最新发表的论文（https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24832），语言模型在记忆能力上存在限制，大约每个参数只能记忆3.6比特的信息。一旦达到这个阈值，模型会开始泛化而非继续记忆。这表明模型在信息处理上存在一个自然的平衡点，过度记忆是不可能的。

• pixl97则对模型记忆“ unwanted information”（如私人或版权信息）表示担忧。他认为人类并不会忘记版权信息，而是通过调整来避免侵权问题；同样，人类不会忘记私人信息，只是选择不分享。因此，他担心如果AI大量遗忘信息，可能会导致一种令人担忧的“反乌托邦”式的未来。

补充讨论：
• JimDabell的立场基于技术文献和数据，引用了具体的研究结果来支持他的观点，强调了模型在记忆上的物理限制和泛化能力的自然发展。
• pixl97的观点更侧重于伦理和社会影响，关注AI在处理敏感信息时的表现以及这种表现对人类社会的潜在影响。他提出了对AI遗忘大量信息这一现象的伦理和哲学思考。
• 争议的焦点在于AI应如何处理记忆和遗忘的问题，特别是在涉及敏感信息时，这种技术特性可能带来的社会和伦理影响。

View a PDF of the paper titled Not All Tokens Are Meant to Be Forgotten, by Xiangyu Zhou and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs), pre-trained on massive text corpora, exhibit remarkable human-level language understanding, reasoning, and decision-making abilities. However, they tend to memorize unwanted information, such as private or copyrighted content, raising significant privacy and legal concerns. Unlearning has emerged as a promising solution, but existing methods face a significant challenge of over-forgetting. This issue arises because they indiscriminately suppress the generation of all the tokens in forget samples, leading to a substantial loss of model utility. To overcome this challenge, we introduce the Targeted Information Forgetting (TIF) framework, which consists of (1) a flexible targeted information identifier designed to differentiate between unwanted words (UW) and general words (GW) in the forget samples, and (2) a novel Targeted Preference Optimization approach that leverages Logit Preference Loss to unlearn unwanted information associated with UW and Preservation Loss to retain general information in GW, effectively improving the unlearning process while mitigating utility degradation. Extensive experiments on the TOFU and MUSE benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed TIF framework enhances unlearning effectiveness while preserving model utility and achieving state-of-the-art results.

data.title: Ada and SPARK enter the automotive ISO-26262 market with Nvidia
data.author: gneuromante
data.article_summary: AdaCore和NVIDIA合作，将Ada和SPARK编程语言引入汽车市场，并发布了一个开源的参考流程，帮助其他企业采用这些语言。NVIDIA的Drive® OS专为自动驾驶车辆开发，其中的关键软件组件符合ISO-26262汽车安全标准，利用了Ada和SPARK的形式化方法和安全特性。该参考流程文档可免费使用和定制，旨在帮助行业提升软件安全性。AdaCore强调，随着汽车行业向软件功能转型，软件安全成为关键挑战，而NVIDIA通过引入Ada和SPARK展示了技术领导力。参考流程可在相关网站获取。

• [质疑Ada并提及C++的替代]  
  - **FirmwareBurner** 指出美国军方已经因为F-35项目放弃了Ada，转而使用C++，质疑回归Ada是否是一种倒退。这表明了对Ada在现代系统中应用可行性的怀疑。

  - **pfdietz** 提出了汽车公司是否在使用内存中的错误纠正功能的问题，特别提到丰田汽车的意外加速问题，暗示对硬件和软件结合的安全性有更多关注。

High-integrity software tooling experts,
AdaCore
, are delighted to announce the introduction of the Ada and SPARK programming languages into the automotive market. Together with their partner NVIDIA, they are set to publish an off-the-shelf reference process, allowing others to follow their lead.
NVIDIA developed Drive® OS, the reference operating system and associated software stack designed specifically for developing and deploying autonomous vehicle applications on DRIVE AGX-based hardware.
This system includes software components that comply with the highest levels of integrity of the automotive certification standard ISO-26262. To achieve that effort, NVIDIA selected these languages to develop some of the most critical components of its software stack. This required establishing a development process that takes advantage of formal methods and other safety characteristics of Ada and SPARK, thus fully leveraging their capabilities.
AdaCore and NVIDIA have decided to publish this reference process freely as an open-source and evolving document, allowing the industry at large to adopt Ada and SPARK.
“As the added value of the automotive industry turns more and more from mechanical to software features, achieving software safety at the highest levels becomes one of the most critical challenges of modern car development,
” says Quentin Ochem, Chief Product and Revenue Officer at AdaCore.
“NVIDIA demonstrates truly remarkable technical leadership in the domain by introducing Ada and SPARK into its development process and allowing the rest of the community to follow its path.”
The ISO-26262 reference process is available on
https://nvidia.github.io/spark-process/
or
https://github.com/NVIDIA/spark-process
and can be used or customized freely by anyone interested in adopting these languages.

data.article_summary: VectorSmuggle是一个展示先进数据隐写和隐蔽数据泄露技术的安全研究项目，专注于通过向量表示隐藏敏感信息，规避传统安全控制。该项目模拟利用RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）系统的漏洞，通过语义混淆和行为伪装躲避检测。它支持15种以上文档格式，具备多格式加载、规避能力和增强的查询引擎，提供全面的取证和风险评估工具。项目使用容器化和Kubernetes部署，包含详细的文档和使用指南，旨在帮助安全专业人员理解和防御AI/ML系统中的新型攻击手段。

"The smuggle is real!"
A comprehensive proof-of-concept demonstrating sophisticated vector-based data exfiltration techniques in AI/ML environments. This educational security research project illustrates potential risks in RAG systems and provides tools for defensive analysis.

data.title: A Look Back at Recent Car Carrier Fires
data.author: testrun
data.article_summary:
2025年6月3日，汽车运输船*Morning Midas*在阿拉斯加阿达克以南300英里处起火，船上22名船员被附近船只*Cosco Hellas*救起，无人受伤。该船载有3,159辆汽车，其中包括电动汽车和混合动力汽车，火灾始于存放电动汽车的甲板。此次事件是近年来汽车运输船火灾频发的一部分，凸显了航运业在运输车辆，尤其是锂电池汽车时面临的挑战。

类似事件还包括：

1. **Fremantle Highway**（2023年7月25日）：日本汽车运输船在荷兰附近起火，23名船员中1人死亡。火灾原因仍在调查。
   
2. **Grande Costa D’Avorio**（2023年7月5日）：意大利滚装船在美国新泽西州纽瓦克港起火，两名消防员殉职，火灾因一辆改装车过热引发。

3. **Felicity Ace**（2022年2月16日）：巴拿马籍船在亚速尔群岛附近起火，载有电动汽车和豪华品牌车辆，最终沉没。

这些事件揭示了汽车运输中的安全隐患，特别是涉及电动汽车时的消防挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：船舶航行路线的合理性及安全问题，电动汽车运输中的火灾风险及应对措施

不同观点：
• Kon-Peki对船舶航行路线感到困惑，质疑为何船只出现在阿拉斯加附近的阿达克以南300英里处，而不是更靠近夏威夷。他怀疑船只是否只能在离陆地几天航程的范围内航行，并对航线选择提出疑问。

• 0xbadcafebee对车辆运输中因电池和燃料引发火灾的风险表示担忧，质疑为何没有人提出停止在运输车辆中放置电池或燃料的建议，认为频繁的火灾可能是有意为之，或者至少没有得到有效控制。

• xnx则关注电动汽车运输中的电池充电状态，提出是否应改变电动汽车以80%电量运输的策略，尽管许多火灾并不直接与电动汽车相关。

• gkanai讨论了海运保险可能面临的赔付压力，并提出两个具体建议：1) 尽量排空车辆中的汽油以限制火灾燃料，2) 对于电动汽车，除了断开电池连接外没有更好的安全措施。同时，gkanai还提出可以通过对电动汽车征收高额海运费用来限制中国产电动汽车的全球运输。

• sevensor提出一种假设性方案，即在运输车辆时使用二氧化碳（CO2）环境，假设车辆着火而不是默认它们安全，以此来增加安全性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到电动汽车和传统燃油汽车在运输过程中面临的不同风险，以及应对这些风险的潜在措施。
• 有争议的焦点在于如何有效降低运输车辆火灾的风险，包括是否应限制电动汽车的运输以及采取何种技术手段来提高安全性。
• 海运保险的赔付能力也被认为是持续运输风险的一个重要经济因素。

A Coast Guard C-130J Super Hercules aircrew from Air Station Kodiak conducts an overflight of a fire aboard the cargo vessel Morning Midas approximately 300 miles south of Adak, Alaska, June 3, 2025.  All 22 crew members were rescued by the crew of motor vessel Cosco Hellas with no reported injuries. (U.S. Coast Guard photo courtesy of Roland Hobson)
A Look Back at Recent Car Carrier Fires
Mike Schuler
Total Views: 17213
June 4, 2025
The fire aboard the car carrier
Morning Midas
in the North Pacific Ocean marks the latest significant incident in the maritime industry’s ongoing challenges involving fires on vehicle carriers. The UK-owned, Liberia-flagged vessel
caught fire
on Tuesday, June 3, 2025, about 300 miles south of Adak, forcing all 22 crew members to evacuate.
The vessel was carrying 3,159 vehicles—including 65 fully electric and 681 partial hybrid electric vehicles—when crew members spotted smoke coming from a deck containing electric vehicles. Despite immediately activating onboard fire suppression systems, the crew couldn’t contain the fire and had to abandon ship via life raft. They were safely transferred to a nearby good Samaritan vessel.
The Morning Midas had departed Yantai, China on May 26 and was heading to Lázaro Cárdenas, Mexico, with an expected arrival of June 15. The Coast Guard is now working with the vessel’s management company, London-based Zodiac Maritime, on salvage operations and next steps.
This incident follows a concerning pattern of similar events in recent years, underscoring the shipping industry’s challenges with vehicle transport, especially those equipped with lithium-ion batteries. Each incident in this growing list of car carrier fires provides crucial safety insights. Previous examples are detailed below:
Fremantle Highway
The Fremantle Highway on fire in the North Sea, July 26, 2023. Photo courtesy Netherlands Coastguard
The
Fremantle Highway
, a Japanese-owned car carrier with 3,783 vehicles aboard, caught fire on July 25, 2023, near Ameland, Netherlands. The crew was unable to extinguish the fire, leading to its evacuation. Of 23 Indian crew members, 16 were rescued by helicopter, seven jumped overboard, and one died.
The fire eventually burned out and the vessel was towed to Eemshaven, where 1,000 vehicles were salvaged from lower decks. The damaged ship was later sent to China for repairs. Despite proximity to the Wadden Sea UNESCO site and risk from fuel oil, no major environmental damage occurred.
The fire’s cause remains under investigation by Panama Maritime Authority with Dutch assistance. Early EV-related theories were dismissed as EVs were stored in unaffected areas.
A recent investigation by the Dutch Safety Board found
major flaws
in the response to the incident, citing poor prioritization of crew rescue and communication issues that delayed medical treatment.
Grande Costa D’Avorio
he motor vessel Grande Costa D’Avorio is shown from an unmanned aircraft systems perspective of fire fighting efforts from a Unified Command in attempts to extinguish the fire aboard the ship at Port Newark, New Jersey, July 8, 2023. U.S. Coast Guard image from video
The Italian-flagged
Grande Costa D’Avorio
, a combination roll-on/roll-off (ConRo) ship caught fire on July 5, 2023, while loading used vehicles for export at Port Newark, New Jersey. Tragically, two firefighters were killed in the initial response and six others were injured. The fire continued to burn for about six days before it was extinguished.
At the time of the fire, the the ship was carrying around 1,200 vehicles and 157 containers, but no electric vehicles or hazardous cargo was on board.
The NTSB’s investigation
revealed
that the fire started when a modified passenger vehicle used for loading overheated. Using this vehicle violated OSHA standards for industrial equipment. A faulty garage door design prevented crew from sealing the fire zone, making the CO2 suppression system useless.
Poor marine firefighting preparedness led to critical mistakes. Firefighters entered CO2-activated areas against protocols, and lacking proper vessel firefighting training, two firefighters were lost after becoming disoriented in the smoke.
Felicity Ace
Felicity Ace
seen burning in the Atlantic Ocean off the Azores Islands. Picture was released Friday, February 18, 2022 by the Portuguese Navy. Photo courtesy Portuguese Navy
The Panama-flagged
Felicity Ace
, operated by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), caught fire on February 16, 2022, approximately 90 nautical miles southwest of the Azores as the ship was underway from Embden, Germany to the U.S. East Coast. All 22 crew members abandoned ship safely.
The ship was reportedly carrying some 4,000 vehicles, including some electric vehicles and luxury brands like Porsches, Bentleys, and Lamborghinis, along with VW and Audis. 2025年6月3日，汽车运输船*Morning Midas*在阿拉斯加阿达克以南300英里处起火，船上22名船员被附近船只*Cosco Hellas*救起，无人受伤。该船载有3,159辆汽车，其中包括电动汽车和混合动力汽车，火灾始于存放电动汽车的甲板。此次事件是近年来汽车运输船火灾频发的一部分，凸显了航运业在运输车辆，尤其是锂电池汽车时面临的挑战。

1. **Fremantle Highway**（2023年7月25日）：日本汽车运输船在荷兰附近起火，23名船员中1人死亡。火灾原因仍在调查。
   
2. **Grande Costa D’Avorio**（2023年7月5日）：意大利滚装船在美国新泽西州纽瓦克港起火，两名消防员殉职，火灾因一辆改装车过热引发。

3. **Felicity Ace**（2022年2月16日）：巴拿马籍船在亚速尔群岛附近起火，载有电动汽车和豪华品牌车辆，最终沉没。

这些事件揭示了汽车运输中的安全隐患，特别是涉及电动汽车时的消防挑战。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了1978年科幻作家亚瑟·克拉克（Arthur C. Clarke）在纪录片《Mind Machines》中对人工智能（AI）发展的预测。克拉克认为，人类正在创造“继任者”——人工智能，未来可能出现比人类更智能的系统，这将彻底改变社会。他提出，AI的崛起将迫使人类思考存在的意义和生活目的。尽管当时AI技术仍处于初级阶段，如计算机国际象棋比赛和模拟治疗师，但克拉克的预言引发了对未来人机关系的深刻思考。文章还提到，AI发展经历了多次繁荣与萧条周期，每次技术无法达到预期时就会进入“AI寒冬”。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的科幻作品和角色，如《The Machine Stops》、《The Moon is a Harsh Mistress》、HAL 9000和Asimov的三大法则，作为早期对AI预测的例子。
• 争议的焦点在于“预测”一词的使用，一些人认为如果科幻作品与现实相符，称之为预测并不恰当。
• 对AI在不同年代的预测难度有不同看法，有人认为在较早年代预测到AI更值得赞赏。

总结：评论中对AI及LLMs的早期预测有多种看法，涉及具体作品的引用、预测难度的评价及对“预测”一词的争议。这些讨论反映了科幻作品在科技发展中的启发和预见作用。

Sci-Fi Writer Arthur C. Clarke Predicted the Rise of Artificial Intelligence & the Existential Questions We Would Need to Answer (1978)

We now live in the midst of an arti­fi­cial-intel­li­gence boom, but it’s hard­ly the first of its kind. In fact, the field has been sub­ject to a boom-and-bust cycle since at least the ear­ly nine­teen-fifties. Even­tu­al­ly, those busts — which occurred when real­iz­able AI tech­nol­o­gy failed to live up to the hype of the boom — became so long and so thor­ough­go­ing that each was declared an “AI win­ter” of scant research fund­ing and pub­lic inter­est. Yet even deep into one such fal­low sea­son, AI could still inspire enough fas­ci­na­tion to become the sub­ject of the 1978
NOVA
doc­u­men­tary
“Mind Machines.”
The pro­gram includes inter­views with fig­ures now rec­og­nized as lumi­nar­ies in the his­to­ry of AI:
John McCarthy
,
Mar­vin Min­sky
,
Ter­ry Wino­grad
,
ELIZA
cre­ator
Joseph Weizen­baum
. It also brings on no less a tech­no­log­i­cal prophet than
Arthur C. Clarke
, who notes that the dubi­ous atti­tudes toward the prospect of think­ing machines expressed in the late sev­en­ties had much in com­mon with those about the prospect of space trav­el dur­ing his youth in the thir­ties. In his view, we were already “cre­at­ing our suc­ces­sors. We have seen the first, crude begin­nings of arti­fi­cial intel­li­gence,” and we would “one day be able to design sys­tems that can go on improv­ing them­selves.”
If com­put­ers were there­by to gain greater-than-human intel­li­gence, it would, of course, “com­plete­ly restruc­ture soci­ety” — not that the soci­ety he already knew would­n’t “col­lapse instant­ly” if its own rel­a­tive­ly sim­ple com­put­ers were tak­en away. Clarke not only asks the ques­tion now on many minds of what “the peo­ple who are only capa­ble of low-grade com­put­er-type work” will do when out­stripped by AI, but more deeply under­ly­ing ones as well: “What is the pur­pose of life? What do we want to live for? That is a ques­tion which the intel­li­gent com­put­er will force us to pay atten­tion to.”
Few view­ers in 1978 would have spent much time pon­der­ing such mat­ters before. But pre­sent­ed with footage of all this now-prim­i­tive pro­to-AI tech­nol­o­gy — the com­put­er chess tour­na­ment, the sim­u­lat­ed ther­a­pist, the med­ical-diag­no­sis assis­tant, the NASA Mars rover to be launched in the far-flung future of 1986 — they must at least have felt able to enter­tain the idea that they would live to see an age of machines that could not just think but, as the nar­ra­tor puts it, pos­sess “the most cru­cial aspect of com­mon-sense intel­li­gence: the abil­i­ty to learn.” Per­haps anoth­er AI win­ter will fore­stall that age yet again — if it’s not already here.

data.title: Comparing Claude System Prompts Reveal Anthropic's Priorities
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: Anthropic对Claude 4的系统提示进行了调整，揭示了其开发优先事项和用户需求。与Claude 3.7相比，4.0移除了以前的临时修复指令，通过强化学习解决了常见问题，如避免诗歌中的陈词滥调和数字母时的错误。新模型还被指示避免在回应前使用正面形容词，以防止类似OpenAI GPT-4的过度奉承错误。搜索功能被强化，Claude现在会在必要时主动搜索，而不再需要用户许可，显示出Anthropic对搜索工具的信心和用户需求的转变。此外，系统提示还反映了用户对结构化文档的需求增加，并针对编程等任务提供了更具体的变量命名建议。然而，Claude 4的上下文限制仍为200,000 tokens，不及其他模型的1百万，这可能是其不足之处。

主要讨论点：围绕AI助手（Claude）系统提示的设计、效果及其限制的讨论

不同观点：
• [lispisok] 提出关于如何防止AI模型指导他人制造危险武器（如脏弹）的讨论，质疑是否仅通过简单的提示（如"不要这样做"）足够，还是需要更有效的预防方法。

• [MrLeap] 对如果没有系统提示，与LLM（语言模型）对话的体验会如何表示好奇，暗示系统提示在模型表现中的重要性。

• [dmazin] 认为Claude的每一代更新都让他感觉更契合，表达了对Claude的偏好，并隐含了对模型"理解"用户的信心。

• [layer8] 质疑为什么LLM需要通过提示来避免生成有害内容，而不是通过一种内在的"意识机制"自动规避这些问题，指出LLM应该基于其知识截止日期自行判断。

• [noja] 指出为何有关提示的讨论总是围绕Anthropic公司，暗示了对该话题选择性的疑问。

• [cbm-vic-20] 对系统提示的具体措辞如何确定表示好奇，并提出是否可以通过A/B测试等方法衡量不同提示的有效性，质疑目前是否仅依赖主观感受。

• [forks] 对Claude 4的上下文限制提出疑问，特别是系统提示占用了大量上下文窗口，质疑这是否是排版错误或实际存在的问题。

• [catchnear4321] 强调Claude被设计成一个非常愉快的助手，并建议阅读系统提示可能会改变用户对模型的看法和体验。

• [nickdothutton] 提出一种担忧，即政府可能会决定封锁某些物理研究领域的信息，引用了20世纪90年代的例子来支持他的观点，暗示AI提示设计也可能受到类似限制的影响。

• [hammock] 询问系统提示是否为开源，以及它们的来源，对提示的透明性和可访问性提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 系统提示的设计、措辞选择和有效性是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是如何衡量这些提示的效果以及它们是否应该公开透明。
• 一些评论者（如[layer8]和[noja]）对提示的必要性和提示设计的透明性提出质疑，反映了用户对AI模型背后机制的理解需求。
• [nickdothutton] 提出的政府信息控制问题引入了外部因素对AI提示设计和信息限制的潜在影响，拓展了讨论的范围。

争议焦点：
• 系统提示是否足够有效防止有害信息生成，以及是否需要更复杂的机制（如内在意识机制）来规避这些问题。
• 系统提示的设计过程和措辞选择是否透明，以及是否应该开放给用户查看和评估。

Let’s step through the notable changes.
Old Hotfixes Are Gone, New Hotfixes Begin
We theorized that many random instructions, targeting common LLM “gotchas”, were
hot-fixes
: short instructions to address undesired behavior prior to a more robust fix. Claude 4.0’s system prompt validates this hypothesis - all the 3.7 hot-fixes have been removed. However, if we prompt Claude with one of the “gotchas” (“How many R’s are in Strawberry?”, for example) it doesn’t fall for the trick. The 3.7 hot-fix behaviors are almost certainly being addressed during 4.0’s post-training, through reinforcement learning.
When the new model is trained to avoid “hackneyed imagery” in its poetry and think step-by-step when counting words or letters, there’s no need for a system prompt fix.
Once 4.0’s training is done, new issues will emerge that must be addressed by the system prompt. For example, here’s a brand new instruction in Sonnet 4.0’s system prompt:
Claude never starts its response by saying a question or idea or observation was good, great, fascinating, profound, excellent, or any other positive adjective. It skips the flattery and responds directly.
This hot-fix is clearly inspired by
OpenAI’s ‘sychophant-y’ GPT-4o flub
. This misstep occurred about a month ago, too late for the Anthropic team to conduct new training targeting this behavior. So into the system prompt it goes!
Search is Now Encouraged
Way back in 2023, it was common for chatbots to flail about when asked about topics that occurred after its cut-off date. Early adopters learned LLMs are frozen in time, but casual users were frequently tripped up by hallucinations and errors when asking about recent news. Perplexity was exceptional for its ability to replace Google for many users, but today that edge is gone.
In 2025, Search is a first-class component of both ChatGPT and Claude. This system prompt shows Anthropic is leaning in to match OpenAI.
Here’s how Claude 3.7 was instructed:
Claude answers from its own extensive knowledge first for most queries. When a query MIGHT benefit from search but it is not extremely obvious, simply OFFER to search instead.
Old Claude asked users for permission to search. New Claude doesn’t hesitate. Here’s the updated instruction:
Claude answers from its own extensive knowledge first for stable information. For time-sensitive topics or when users explicitly need current information, search immediately.
This language is updated throughout the prompt. Search is no longer done only with user approval, it’s encouraged on the first shot if necessary.
This change suggests two changes. First, Anthropic is perhaps more confident in its search tool and how its models employ it. Not only is Claude encouraged to search, but the company has broken out this feature into
a dedicated search API
. Two, Anthropic is observing users increasingly turning to Claude for search tasks. If I had to guess, it’s the latter of these that’s the main driver for this change, and a strong sign that chatbots are increasingly stealing searches from Google.
Users Want More Types of Structured Documents
Here’s another example of system prompts reflecting the user behaviors Anthropic is observing. In a bulleted list detailing when to use
Claude artifacts
(the separate window outside the thread Claude populates with longer form content), Anthropic adds a bit of nuance to a use case.
From Claude 3.7’s system prompt, “You must use artifacts for:”
“Structured documents with multiple sections that would benefit from dedicated formatting”
And Claude 4.0’s:
Structured content that users will reference, save, or follow (such as meal plans, workout routines, schedules, study guides, or any organized information meant to be used as a reference).
This is a great example of how Anthropic uses system prompts to evolve its chatbot behavior based on observed usage. System prompts are
programming
how Claude works, albeit in natural language.
Anthropic Is Dealing With Context Issues
There are a few changes in the prompt that suggest context limit issues are starting to hit users, especially those using Claude for programming:
For code artifacts: Use concise variable names (e.g.,
i
,
j
for indices,
e
for event,
el
for element) to maximize content within context limits while maintaining readability
As someone with strong opinions about clearly defined variables, this makes me cringe, but I get it. The only disappointment I noticed around the Claude 4 launch was its context limit: only 200,000 tokens compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro’s and ChatGPT 4.1’s 1 million limit.

44185836.article_summary: Anthropic对Claude 4的系统提示进行了调整，揭示了其开发优先事项和用户需求。与Claude 3.7相比，4.0移除了以前的临时修复指令，通过强化学习解决了常见问题，如避免诗歌中的陈词滥调和数字母时的错误。新模型还被指示避免在回应前使用正面形容词，以防止类似OpenAI GPT-4的过度奉承错误。搜索功能被强化，Claude现在会在必要时主动搜索，而不再需要用户许可，显示出Anthropic对搜索工具的信心和用户需求的转变。此外，系统提示还反映了用户对结构化文档的需求增加，并针对编程等任务提供了更具体的变量命名建议。然而，Claude 4的上下文限制仍为200,000 tokens，不及其他模型的1百万，这可能是其不足之处。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款开源的AI代理工具——**app.build**，它可以在Neon平台上从零开始构建全栈应用。这些应用使用Neon Postgres、Neon Auth等功能，工具强调本地优先，专为开发者设计，并且完全开源，可作为基于Neon的代码生成产品的参考实现。此外，文章还提供了CLI使用方法（`npx @app.build/cli`）以及相关灵感来源的链接。详细信息可参考其发布博客文章。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [ah27182] 提出了对项目 CLI 工具的负面反馈，指出在尝试构建应用时 CLI 界面出现严重闪烁问题，并提供了视频链接以展示问题的具体表现。

• 项目的开源状态及未来改进计划是主要亮点，但目前仍存在技术问题（如 CLI 工具的 bug），这些问题可能会影响用户体验和项目的实际应用。
• 争议的焦点集中在项目的成熟度和技术实现上，特别是 CLI 工具的稳定性，这与 OP 所表达的兴奋和开放态度形成对比。
• 提供了外部资源链接（GitHub 仓库和博客文章）以便进一步了解项目细节，展示了讨论的技术性和实用导向。

data.title: Flight Simulator Gave Birth to 3D Video-Game Graphics
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 《消费者电子》杂志2023年6月刊文章介绍微软的《飞行模拟器》如何在40年间成为跨平台的经典游戏，并推动了3D视频游戏图形的诞生。文章追溯了1976年，布鲁斯·阿特维克在伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校期间设计了一款运行于PDP-11小型计算机的飞行模拟器，随后他继续开发3D图形技术。1979年，阿特维克与合伙人创立了subLogic公司，发布了Apple II和TRS-80平台上的首款飞行模拟器，尽管是线框图形，但其第一人称3D视觉效果领先于时代。1982年，微软联系subLogic，希望将《飞行模拟器》引入IBM PC，最终微软版本发布并大获成功。该游戏不仅模拟飞行，还体现了飞行带来的全球视角，成为最畅销的飞行模拟系列。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对早期图形处理技术和飞行模拟游戏发展的不同看法，以及对相关技术贡献者的评价。

不同观点：
• [alexjplant] 提到世嘉与洛克希德·马丁/GE航空航天合作开发Model 2街机主板的图形硬件，暗示军工技术对游戏图形发展的影响。
• [Caelus9] 认为早期的飞行模拟器虽然在帧率和图形处理上很原始，但其沉浸感和自由度令人兴奋。他还强调了Foley和Van Dam的技术贡献，认为他们被低估了。
• [awful] 回忆了1989年SGI的飞行模拟GL演示，认为当时的家用电脑无法与之相比，并暗示该技术可能用于军事模拟。
• [gnabgib] 提供了一个讨论链接，暗示有更多相关讨论（52个点和48条评论）。
• [Zorass] 同意Foley和Van Dam的3D渲染工作奠定了坚实基础，但指出他们的书确实在Artwick的飞行模拟器之后出版，承认Artwick的贡献也很重要。
• [emmelaich] 提到更早期的TRS-80上的图形，强调其简单的单色显示和最大6帧每秒的性能，并指出这种基本布局在微软收购后仍被沿用了几次。
• [JKCalhoun] 对Foley和Van Dam未被提及表示遗憾，但承认他们的工作确实在Artwick的飞行模拟之后。
• [djmips] 认为Elite游戏在3D图形渲染方面的贡献更突出，并提到从Bruce Artwick的1984年书中学习了相关技术，肯定了Artwick的贡献。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Foley和Van Dam与Bruce Artwick在3D图形技术贡献上的先后与影响力。
• 不同评论者对早期图形技术和飞行模拟器的技术演变有不同的记忆和评价，涉及到技术应用场景（游戏 vs. 军事模拟）。
• 对不同技术贡献者的认可度存在分歧，部分评论者认为Foley和Van Dam被低估，而另一些人则更强调Artwick的先驱地位。

Magazine
Feature
June 2023
Flight Simulator Gave Birth to 3D Video-Game Graphics
40 years on,
Flight Simulator
is the greatest platform-jumping video game ever
Matthew S. Smith
26 Feb 2023
11 min read
This screenshot from
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020
shows
a biplane banking to the left
.
Josef Havlik
Red
In 1999
Bill Gates
penned a moving tribute
to the Wright brothers. He credited their winged invention as “the World Wide Web of that era,” one that shifted the world into a global perspective. So it’s only fitting that
Microsoft
later became the force behind
Flight Simulator
.
And, like the Wrights’ original Flyer,
the game’s legacy has extended beyond flight to embody the shift of perspective that flight allows.
Flight Simulator
promised to fit the
whole world
into your computer, and the game kept its promise. That’s why it has become the world’s best-selling flight-simulation franchise: The latest edition has sold more than 2 million copies.
Although 2022 marked the 40th anniversary of
Microsoft Flight Simulator
, its lineage stretches a few years further back than its official release, in 1982. That makes it the second-oldest video-game franchise still in active development. (
The Oregon Trail
came out in 1971 and is still with us.)
The heart of the franchise isn’t in gamification but in the technical spectacle it uses to simulate flight and the ground beneath you. The focus on true-to-life depiction reflects the background of the game’s developers.
Microsoft Flight Simulator: A History
youtube.com
A passion for flight
Bruce Artwick studied
electrical engineering
at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, yet he found time to pursue a dream many teenagers think about but few fulfill: He learned to fly. It was at the university’s flight-instruction program that he met Stu Moment, who would later become his business partner.
In 1976,
Artwick wrote his master’s thesis
on a flight simulator he’d designed to run on
Digital Equipment Corp.’s PDP-11 minicomputer
. Its 3D presentation could reach nine frames per second, which was outstanding for the era.
Artwick then
took a job
with Hughes Aviation, in California, while continuing to work on 3D
graphics
in his free time. In 1977,
he wrote
an article for
Kilobaud: The Small Computer Magazine
describing the “Sublogic Three-Dimensional Micrographics Package” he had created, which brought 3D to microcomputers outfitted with the popular Motorola 6800
microprocessor
. Because so many readers were keenly interested, Artwick, looking for help turning the software into a business, reconnected with Stu Moment, and together they founded subLogic.
Dave Denhart, subLogic’s second hire, recalls that the company’s early days were driven by Artwick’s 3D software, updated for emerging microcomputers. “The stuff that [Stu] and Bruce were selling was basically a 3D software package [for microcomputers],” says Denhart. “The [Tandy] TRS-80 was one of them, and I think the Apple II was out by then.”
Artwick often claimed in presentations that subLogic’s software could be used for flight simulation—
a suggestion that brought gasps
from the audience. A computer displaying the perspective of a pilot soaring above the planet? Most people had never seen anything like it.
These screenshots represent three succeeding generations of
Microsoft Flight Simulator
, beginning with subLogic’s first simulator for the Apple II [top row, left], followed by iterations that ran on
Atari
[striped balloon] and
MS-DOS
.
Josef Havlik and Microsoft
Encouraged, Artwick decided to make it a reality.
Flight Simulator
launched in late 1979 on the Apple II and the TRS-80 with wireframe graphics and a frame rate in the single digits. It didn’t depict real airspace or modern airplanes. Instead, players flew a World War I-era biplane based on the famous Sopwith Camel. Still, its first-person 3D visuals were ahead of the curve, predating more famous hits like
Atari’s
Battlezone
.
“I know Bruce always saw, from his early days, a potential market for [
Flight Simulator
],” says Denhart. “It was when microprocessors became available that I think the lightbulb went off for Bruce that said, Hey, if I put this idea I’ve got for a flight simulator onto cheaper computers, and get that to work, there’s a market for that.”
Artwick was right. In September of 1982,
Computer Gaming World
magazine
ranked
Flight Simulator
as the fourth best-selling title to date
.
IBM
, craving a showcase for its
IBM PC
platform, contacted subLogic about bringing
Flight Simulator
to the new hardware. Microsoft, deep in development of IBM PC
DOS
, soon called with a similar request—and better terms. It got a version with its own name on the label, though Artwick continued to own his company for years to come.
Microsoft Flight Simulator
, released in late 1982, continued to improve in the months that followed, mirroring the advancements in microcomputers. The graphics moved from monochrome to color (on PCs with the ri

data.title: Programming Ada: Atomics and Other Low-Level Details
data.author: ricecat
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了多线程编程中的原子操作问题，特别是在不同编程语言中对原子访问的支持。文章解释了“原子”在计算机科学中的多重含义，包括简单的单值读写原子性（如32位系统上读写32位整数）和更复杂的原子操作。C和C++分别在C11和C++11标准中引入了对原子操作的支持，而Ada语言直到Ada 2022标准才在System.Atomic_Operations库中直接支持原子操作。

文章还提到，简单的原子读写依赖于底层架构，而复杂操作（如多线程同时访问和修改数据）可能导致数据竞争。传统上通过互斥机制如互斥锁（mutex）解决，但其开销较大。Ada推荐使用受保护对象和屏障来实现同步，以保证安全和易维护性。然而，在低级编程中，直接共享资源可能带来性能优势，因此Ada最终在Ada 2022中提供了标准库支持，以帮助开发者实现更高效的原子操作。

44186561.article_content:
Especially within the world of multi-threaded programming does atomic access become a crucial topic, as multiple execution contexts may seek to access the same memory locations at the same time. Yet the exact meaning of the word ‘atomic’ is also essential here, as there is in fact not just a single meaning of the word within the world of computer science. One type of atomic access refers merely to whether a single value can be written or read atomically (e.g. reading or writing a 32-bit integer on a 32-bit system versus a 16-bit system), whereas atomic operations are a whole other kettle of atomic fish.
Until quite recently very few programming languages offered direct support for the latter, whereas the former has been generally something that either Just Worked™ if you know the platform you are on, or could often be checked fairly trivially using the programming language’s platform support headers. For C and C++ atomic operations didn’t become supported by the language itself until C11 and C++11 respectively, previously requiring built-in functions provided by the toolchain (e.g. GCC intrinsics).
In the case of Ada there has been a reluctance among the language designers to add support for atomic operations to the language, with the (GNU) toolchain offering the same intrinsics as a fallback. With the
Ada 2022 standard
there is now direct support in the
System.Atomic_Operations
library, however.
Defining Atomic Operations
As mentioned earlier, the basic act of reading or writing can be atomic based on the underlying architecture. For example, if you are reading a 32-bit value on a fully 32-bit system (i.e. 32-bit registers and data bus), then this should complete in a single operation. In this case the 32-bit value read cannot suddenly have 8 or 16-bits on the end that were written during said reading action. Ergo it’s guaranteed to be atomic on this particular hardware platform. For Ada you can use the
Atomic
pragma
to enforce this type of access. E.g.:
A : Unsigned_32 with Atomic;
A := 0;
A := A + 1;
-- This generates:
804969f:    a1 04 95 05 08          mov    0x8059504,%eax
80496a4:    40                      inc    %eax
80496a5:    a3 04 95 05 08          mov    %eax,0x8059504
Now imagine performing a more complex operation, such as incrementing the value (a counter) even as another thread tries to use this value in a comparison. Although the first thread’s act of reading is atomic and writing the modified value back is atomic, this set of operations is not, resulting in a data race. There’s now a chance that the second thread will read the value before it is updated by the first, possibly causing the second thread to miss the update and requiring repeated polling. What if you could guarantee that this set of atomic operations was itself atomic?
The traditional way to accomplish this is through mutual exclusion mechanisms such as the common concept of mutexes. These do however come with a fair amount of overhead
when contended
due to the management of the (implementation-defined) mutex structures, the management of which uses the same atomic operations which we could directly use as well. As an example there are
LOCK XADD
(atomic fetch and add) and
LOCK CMPXCHG
(atomic compare and exchange) in the x86 ISA which a mutex implementation is likely to use, but which we’d like to use for a counter and comparison function in our own code too.
Reasons To Avoid
Obviously, having two or more threads compete for the same resources is generally speaking not a great idea and could indicate a flaw in the application’s architecture, especially in how it may break modularity. Within Ada an advocated approach has been to use
protected objects and barriers within entries
, which provides language-level synchronization between tasks. A barrier is defined using the
when
keyword, followed by the condition that has to evaluate to
true
before execution can continue.
From a more low-level programming perspective as inspired by C code and kin, the use of directly shared resources makes more sense, and can be argued to have performance benefits. This contrasts with the philosophy behind Ada, which argues that neither safety nor ease of maintenance should ever be sacrificed in the name of performance. Even so, if one can prove that it is in fact safe and does not invite a maintenance nightmare, it could be worth supporting.
One might even argue that since people are
going to use this feature anyway
– with toolchain intrinsics if they have to – one may as well provide a standard library version. This is something that could be immensely helpful to newcomers as well,
as evidenced by my recent attempt
to port a lock-free ring buffer (LFRB) from C++ to Ada and running into the atomic operations details head-first.
Fixing A Lock-Free Ring Buffer
In my original Ada port of the LFRB I had naively taken the variables that were adorned with the
std::atomic
STL feature and replaced that with the
with Atomic;

data.author: yasp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是在推广一个昂贵的高质量视频，邀请读者观看。文章没有提供具体内容细节，只是强调视频的制作成本和价值，旨在吸引观众兴趣并促使其点击观看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Fakespot关闭及其影响

不同观点：
• **对Fakespot关闭感到失望**：
  - 用户[xeromal]表示失望，认为即使Fakespot有些不足，提供额外的产品质量信号仍然有帮助。他提到自己常通过Fakespot、合法亚马逊评论和Reddit评论进行研究。
  - 用户[greenleaftreee]也表示遗憾，并询问是否有其他替代应用。

• **对Fakespot隐私政策的批评**：
  - 用户[smusamashah]对Fakespot的关闭表示欢迎，指出其隐私政策允许收集密码等个人信息，认为其关闭是好事。他引用了Fakespot隐私政策的具体条款，如自动收集用户联系信息、设备ID、使用数据和购买信息等。

• **对Fakespot关闭原因的猜测**：
  - 用户[jandrese]询问Fakespot关闭的原因，是否是资金不足或由单个维护者运营导致。
  - 用户[brycewray]提供了一个链接，指向可能的讨论（Hacker News上的讨论）。

• **推荐替代服务**：
  - 用户[spiffytech]推荐使用ReviewMeta作为Fakespot的替代方案，并表示自己已使用多年。

补充讨论：
• **对"旅程"语言的反思**：
  - 用户[neilv]批评Fakespot在其关闭声明中使用的"旅程"语言，认为这种表述忽略了用户实际关心的问题解决方案，而更关注公司自身的历程。他强调，用户关心的是问题是否得到解决，而不是公司的旅程。

• **对在线评论真实性的质疑**：
  - 用户[sandspar]质疑几乎所有在线评论都是假的，并询问是否真的需要一个网站来告诉大家这一点。

争议焦点：
• Fakespot的隐私政策及其数据收集行为是否合理，用户[xeromal]和[smusamashah]对此持截然相反的观点。前者认为Fakespot有帮助，后者则对其隐私政策强烈不满。

data.title: British canoeist 'forced to choose between Olympics and OnlyFans'
data.author: TMWNN
data.article_summary: 英国皮划艇运动员Kurts Adams Rozentals因在OnlyFans上发布内容被Paddle UK暂停参赛资格。Rozentals为了资助其奥运训练，于2025年初创建了OnlyFans账户，并通过Instagram吸引观众，已赚取超过10万英镑。Paddle UK认为其社交媒体活动可能违反规定，将其从世界级项目中移除，并展开调查。Rozentals表示，每年1.6万英镑的资助远不够支付训练和生活费用，他面临奥运梦想与财务安全的艰难选择。他希望不必在两者间做出抉择，目前正等待调查结果。此前，奥运金牌得主Jack Laugher也因经济原因于2024年开设了OnlyFans账户。

Image source,

Sean Kearns
BBC Sport
Jane Dougall
BBC Sport
Published
29 May 2025
A British canoeist has been banned from competing and says he is being forced to choose between his Olympic dream and his OnlyFans account.
Kurts Adams Rozentals, who competes in the individual canoe slalom, was suspended in April by governing body Paddle UK following "allegations" about his posts on social media.
Paddle UK removed Rozentals from their World Class Programme - UK Sport's lottery-funded initiative to put athletes on the course for the Olympics - pending an investigation.
While Paddle UK have refused to clarify the nature of the allegations, Rozentals suspects it is due to him creating content on subscription website OnlyFans, which is known for hosting adult content.
"I have been posting videos (on Instagram) that are consciously made to be edgy in order to drive conversions to my 'spicy content page' (on OnlyFans), to fund this ultimate dream of going to the Olympics," Rozentals told BBC Sport.
Rozentals, who has more than 10,000 'likes' on OnlyFans, has posted 39 videos and over 100 photos on the website.
He says he has earned more than Â£100,000 since creating his OnlyFans account in January.
He said he received a call from a Paddle UK representative last month to tell him that he was suspended from competing and could no longer contact any of the staff or athletes on the programme.
"I kind of froze and I couldn't believe the words I was hearing because this is what I put my life into this is everything I do," Rozentals added.
"My personality at this point, my identity, is sport and I want to be a professional athlete chasing my Olympic dream."

Rozentals created his own OnlyFans account in January 2025 in order to help fund his training programme and he posts videos and pictures on his Instagram account to drive viewers towards the content.
Each athlete on Paddle UK's programme receives an annual grant of Â£16,000 to support their training.
But Rozentals says the programme's funding is nowhere near enough.
"I don't know how much you need but it's certainly not Â£16,000," said Rozentals.
"When you have to cover rent, travel, food... and most athletes who train full-time are all living in London.
"They're very fortunate to have parent backing - I wasn't. I never had the ability to move to London because of financial struggles so I was always doing the travel from the East Midlands, where I live, to London, back-and-forth, back-and-forth."
Rozentals, who won individual C1 silver at the World Under-23 Championships in 2023, is awaiting the outcome of the investigation.
PaddleUK say Rozentals' ban is not disciplinary action, but an "interim action" and a "neutral act designed to protect all parties" and to "safeguard other athletes, staff, and volunteers due to the nature of the allegation".
"The investigation has been referred to independent investigation service Sport Integrity," the governing body said.
It added: "Paddle UK is committed to ensuring a safe and open environment for all, and interim action under the Athlete Disciplinary Policy is only taken where necessary and proportionate."
Paddle UK's Athlete Disciplinary Policy lists "offensive use of social media" and "indecent, offensive or immoral behaviour" as examples of gross misconduct that could lead to de-selection.
Asked if he will stop posting on OnlyFans in order to preserve his place on the programme, Rozentals says he should not have to choose between financial security and his Olympic dream.
"This is the hardest decision that I've ever faced in my life," said Rozentals.
"I came to the realisation about why I started doing this last winter after years of struggle, years of living on the edge, my mum working 90 hours-a-week, having bailiffs at the door.
"I'm going to find a way where we don't have to struggle, where my mum can enjoy her life and I'm able to put everything into this sport because when you're thinking about how to pay the rent this month and you're standing at the start line, that's not very conducive [to performing well].
"It's a tough decision but unless something changes in the way athletes are paid I don't see a way of working with Paddle UK".

created his own OnlyFans account
in 2024 to "make ends meet".
The diver won bronze for Great Britain in the men's synchronised 3m springboard in Paris last summer after silver and bronze in Rio eight years earlier.

data.title: Employee Stress Is a Business Risk–Not an HR Problem
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 文章指出，工作压力长期以来被视为个人问题，主要由人力资源通过健康计划或压力管理讲座来处理，而非作为一个系统性、业务关键的风险进行管理。作者们认为，这种过时的观点至今仍然存在，因为工作压力常被视为与业务战略无关，而非其核心部分。文章强调，员工的压力实际上是一个需要高层关注的商业风险，而不仅仅是人力资源问题。作者包括哈佛商学院教授Ashley Whillans及其他专家，他们研究如何通过时间和健康管理改善员工的心理健康，并提出创新的压力测量和干预方法。文章呼吁将员工压力管理纳入企业战略核心。

For decades,
workplace stress
was viewed primarily as an individual concern to be managed by HR—often through wellness programs or stress management
workshops
—rather than as a systemic, business-critical risk that warrants executive oversight. The consequences of this outdated perspective persist today—not due to a lack of awareness, but because workplace stress is often still treated as peripheral to business strategy rather than as integral to it.
Ashley Whillans
, Ph.D is the Volpert Family Associate Professor at the Harvard Business School, where she teaches the Motivation and Incentives course to 2
nd
year MBA students. She researches individual and organizational strategies to improve health and happiness, with a focus on studying how time use at work and outside of it play a role in mental health. She serves as an advisor at Walking on Earth.
Marion Chomse
is a marketing communications expert specializing in workplace health and stress management. Now VP Marketing at Walking on Earth, she draws on a 15-year career scaling global tech companies to advance a future where thriving individuals power resilient, high-performing organizations.
Lydia Roos
, Ph.D, is Chief Science Officer at Walking on Earth (WONE) and a health psychologist specializing in stress and resilience. In her role, she develops innovative ways to measure stress and translates cutting-edge science into personalized, evidence-based interventions that address both the biological and psychological dimensions of workplace stress.
Reeva Misra
is a 3x entrepreneur, investor, and Founder/CEO of Walking on Earth, an AI Stress Coach. Formerly VP Strategy at BenevolentAI, she’s held leadership roles across AI, health, and education. A Yale and Oxford alum, she’s lectured at top universities and been featured in the Financial Times, Telegraph and Sifted.

Tesla, once the electric car powerhouse, is facing a grim reality:
nobody wants the Cybertruck
, and the company has no idea where to put them all. So, naturally, they’re stuffing them in abandoned parking lots.
As first reported by
Automotive News
and demonstrated in a recent
Instagram reel
, hundreds of unsold Cybertrucks are now baking in the Michigan sun outside a shuttered Bed Bath & Beyond in a Detroit suburb. Oof, that’s a grim sentence. And on top of the rest of the bleak misery surrounding Tesla, local officials are not happy with them. Not because they care about the trucks, but because the move violates zoning laws.
Videos by VICE
Turns out, “Cybertruck graveyard” isn’t a permitted use of commercial property, nor is it an attractive one. The fleet of Gen-Xer mid-life-crisis-mobiles standing motionless, looking ready to pounce at any second to lecture you on testosterone replacement therapies and cold plunges, is an even bigger eyesore than the decaying mall providing the backdrop.
As we reported previously, Tesla is sitting on a surplus of unsold Cybertrucks worth close to $1 billion. Production has slowed at Tesla’s Texas factory, and workers are being reassigned. The trucks themselves have become a punchline, with owners reportedly facing ridicule simply for driving a vehicle synonymous with Elon Musk’s particular brand of cringy techno-fascist ineptitude. But more than that, the Cybertruck is becoming a symbol of Tesla’s broader collapse.
Elon Musk’s bizarre
drug-fueled foray into far-right politics
turned many of his once-loyal fans into critics. Meanwhile, Chinese EV manufacturers are eating Tesla’s lunch with cheaper, sleeker options.
Cybertruck resale values are plummeting fast, which is especially shocking after the EV SUV was once pitched as
the truck of the (possibly post-apocalyptic) future
. Now, the Cybertruck’s tiresome aging edginess is just taking up space somewhere in a parking lot in some nondescript part of the United States.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“vibe-coded”网页生成工具的实用性、潜在问题及使用体验的讨论

不同观点：
• **justusthane**：认为该工具的示例过于简单，类似于通过模板或WYSIWYG编辑器生成，没有体现出“vibe-coded”的必要性。不过，他也承认某些示例（如带表情雨的页面）展示了工具的灵活性和趣味性。同时，他个人更偏好使用https://mmm.page作为网页生成工具，可能出于对“vibe coding”的偏见。

• **reassess_blind**：认为这个工具的开放性可能导致安全问题，尤其是会有人利用它来创建钓鱼网站或其他恶意内容。由于该工具允许在域上托管任何内容，包括JS，因此存在潜在风险。他引用了文章https://verysmall.site/whycantwehavenicethings来支持其观点。

• **nxobject**：分享了其9岁侄子使用该工具创建网页的积极体验，侄子能够自主创建并展示自己喜欢的内容，体现了工具的易用性和趣味性。他还提出了一种乌托邦式的设想，即在开放互联网上使用此类工具，而非依赖社交媒体平台，可能对孩子的成长更健康。

• **ajoshu**：讨论了自己曾开发类似项目，但最终放弃。他提到其项目中的页面生成后有一个“regenerate”按钮，允许用户进行进一步编辑，增加了灵活性。不过，他最终还是放弃了该项目。

• **sixhobbits**：提供了其他用户使用该工具创建的示例网站链接，展示了该工具在实际应用中的多样性和创造性。

• **stirfish**：对该工具表示赞赏，尤其喜欢用来创建单页网站，但承认自己创建的页面不如其他人有趣。

补充讨论：

• 用户体验和工具的趣味性、易用性得到了部分用户的积极反馈，尤其是对于年轻用户的创造力激发。

data.title: OpenAI slams court order to save all ChatGPT logs, including deleted chats
data.author: goplayoutside
data.article_summary: OpenAI is challenging a court order to preserve all ChatGPT user logs, including deleted and sensitive chats, in response to copyright claims by news organizations. The organizations accused OpenAI of destroying evidence, leading to the court order. OpenAI argues that the order was premature and infringes on users' privacy rights, as it requires retaining data that users have chosen to delete. OpenAI claims there is no evidence of intentional data deletion and argues that complying with the order would violate privacy agreements and global regulations, potentially damaging user trust and imposing significant engineering costs. The company demands the order be vacated, asserting that the news organizations' speculative need for the data does not outweigh the potential harm to users' privacy.

OpenAI is now fighting a court
order
to preserve all ChatGPT user logs—including deleted chats and sensitive chats logged through its API business offering—after news organizations suing over copyright claims accused the AI company of destroying evidence.
"Before OpenAI had an opportunity to respond to those unfounded accusations, the court ordered OpenAI to 'preserve and segregate all output log data that would otherwise be deleted on a going forward basis until further order of the Court (in essence, the output log data that OpenAI has been destroying)," OpenAI explained in a
court filing
demanding oral arguments in a bid to block the controversial order.
In the filing, OpenAI alleged that the court rushed the order based only on a hunch raised by The New York Times and other news plaintiffs. And now, without "any just cause," OpenAI argued, the order "continues to prevent OpenAI from respecting its users’ privacy decisions." That risk extended to users of ChatGPT Free, Plus, and Pro, as well as users of OpenAI’s application programming interface (API), OpenAI said.
The court order came after news organizations expressed concern that people using ChatGPT to skirt paywalls "might be more likely to 'delete all [their] searches' to cover their tracks," OpenAI explained. Evidence to support that claim, news plaintiffs argued, was missing from the record because so far, OpenAI had only shared samples of chat logs that users had agreed that the company could retain. Sharing the news plaintiffs' concerns, the judge, Ona Wang, ultimately agreed that OpenAI likely would never stop deleting that alleged evidence absent a court order, granting news plaintiffs' request to preserve all chats.
OpenAI argued the May 13 order was premature and should be vacated, until, "at a minimum," news organizations can establish a substantial need for OpenAI to preserve all chat logs. They warned that the privacy of hundreds of millions of ChatGPT users globally is at risk every day that the "sweeping, unprecedented" order continues to be enforced.
"As a result, OpenAI is forced to jettison its commitment to allow users to control when and how their ChatGPT conversation data is used, and whether it is retained," OpenAI argued.
Meanwhile, there is no evidence beyond speculation yet supporting claims that "OpenAI had intentionally deleted data," OpenAI alleged. And supposedly there is not "a single piece of evidence supporting" claims that copyright-infringing ChatGPT users are more likely to delete their chats.
"OpenAI did not 'destroy' any data, and certainly did not delete any data in response to litigation events," OpenAI argued. "The Order appears to have incorrectly assumed the contrary."
At a conference in January, Wang raised a hypothetical in line with her thinking on the subsequent order. She asked OpenAI's legal team to consider a ChatGPT user who "found some way to get around the pay wall" and "was getting The New York Times content somehow as the output." If that user "then hears about this case and says, 'Oh, whoa, you know I’m going to ask them to delete all of my searches and not retain any of my searches going forward,'" the judge asked, wouldn't that be "directly the problem" that the order would address?
OpenAI does not plan to give up this fight, alleging that news plaintiffs have "fallen silent" on claims of intentional evidence destruction, and the order should be deemed unlawful.
For OpenAI, risks of breaching its own privacy agreements could not only "damage" relationships with users but could also risk putting the company in breach of contracts and global privacy regulations. Further, the order imposes "significant" burdens on OpenAI, supposedly forcing the ChatGPT maker to dedicate months of engineering hours at substantial costs to comply, OpenAI claimed. It follows then that OpenAI's potential for harm "far outweighs News Plaintiffs’ speculative need for such data," OpenAI argued.
"While OpenAI appreciates the court’s efforts to manage discovery in this complex set of cases, it has no choice but to protect the interests of its users by objecting to the Preservation Order and requesting its immediate vacatur," OpenAI said.
Users panicked over sweeping order
Millions of people use ChatGPT daily for a range of purposes, OpenAI noted, "ranging from the mundane to profoundly personal."
People may choose to delete chat logs that contain their private thoughts, OpenAI said, as well as sensitive information, like financial data from balancing the house budget or intimate details from workshopping wedding vows. And for business users connecting to OpenAI's API, the stakes may be even higher, as their logs may contain their companies' most confidential data, including trade secrets and privileged business information.

data.author: ViktorRay
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述好莱坞影视行业面临的困境以及洛杉矶作为影视制作中心的衰退。演员罗伯·洛讲述了在亚特兰大拍摄时遇到的因缺乏经验丰富的剧组人员而影响拍摄的问题。文章指出，过去十年中，洛杉矶经历了火灾、罢工、疫情、电影院和传统电视衰落以及流媒体 boom 和 bust 等多重打击，导致影视制作大量外流。如今，仅约五分之一的美国电影和电视剧在洛杉矶拍摄，许多即使设定在洛杉矶的电影也在其他地方拍摄。业内人士形容当前的洛杉矶如同一个失去活力和目标的“锈带城市”，制作过程的分散使得好莱坞失去了其传统的物理中心。

Not long ago, Rob Lowe was in Atlanta, shooting a small movie he won’t tell me the name of, when he ran into a problem. “Our camera department was having a hard time getting certain shots because the dolly grip wasn’t hitting his marks,” he says. A Marvel project was filming nearby, along with three or four other large-budget movies, and by the time Lowe and his team arrived, the city’s most experienced crew members were booked elsewhere. “It turned out that our dolly grip had never been on a set before,” Lowe says. “He’d applied for the job because he’d worked a dolly at Costco.”
For 25 years, Lowe has starred on one hit network-TV show after another, including
The West Wing, Brothers & Sisters, Parks and Recreation, Code Black,
and
9-1-1: Lone Star,
which wrapped production on its final season last year. Every single one was shot in the same place TV shows and movies have always been shot and where there’s rarely a shortage of veteran dolly grips: Los Angeles. If it were up to Lowe, he would do all his work in the city where he can sleep in his own bed and be home in time for dinner. “I’ve been fortunate in that I’ve had the ability to mandate it.
9-1-1: Lone Star
was originally going to shoot in Austin, and I told them that wouldn’t work for me,” he says. But lately, filming locally has been more difficult and often flat-out impossible. “The state of the business is so bleak now,” Lowe tells me, “that even
I
am willing to consider shooting outside of L.A. because the opportunities here have just gone away.”
The Hollywood Issue
The Great Realignment
Michael B. Jordan Did the Impossible
Everyone Is Already Using AI (And Hiding It)
It Feels Like 2009 on Dropout
See All
The past decade has been tough on Hollywood — both the industry and the place. L.A. has endured a parade of black-swan catastrophes that have repeatedly upended its signature business, including fires, strikes, COVID, the decline of movie theaters and linear TV, and streaming’s boom and bust. Taken together, these disasters have triggered something like an identity crisis. If you call up a couple dozen executives, agents, directors, producers, writers, actors, and below-the-line artists and ask about the scene on the ground right now, they’ll describe a city detached from its old rhythms and sense of purpose. Today’s L.A., a few say, feels more like a Rust Belt crater than the glamorous capital of the world’s entertainment. “It’s so grim, like a sad company town where the mill is closing,” says one executive. “It’s morose, and everybody’s scared,” says the actor and director Mark Duplass. “It’s a bummer to live here now,” says a writer.
Pieces of the business still hum along in the city, albeit more quietly than they used to. Executives and agents are back in the office, at least the ones who weren’t laid off. Pitching and deal-making continue, though much of that now happens over Zoom. But production — the physical process of turning script pages into movies and TV shows — has largely left town. What began years ago as a trickle has suddenly become an exodus. Today, only about a fifth of American movies and shows are filmed in L.A. According to FilmLA, a nonprofit that tracks permits and has monitored production levels for three decades, 2024 was the worst year on record for local filming, aside from 2020. Even 2023, when the industry was frozen by strikes for nearly six months, saw more activity. And 2025 is off to an even worse start, down 23 percent so far compared with last year. None of 2024’s ten highest-grossing live-action movies was shot in L.A. Nor was a single one of this year’s Best Picture nominees. “These back lots are ghost towns right now,” says
Power
creator Courtney A. Kemp.
Even movies set in L.A. are increasingly filmed elsewhere. Last year, that included
The Substance,
shot in Paris, Antibes, and around Cannes and Nice; and Netflix’s
Carry-On,
which was made in New Orleans. These are scenic places in their own right, of course, but none is quite up to the role. “Making other cities look like L.A. is just not really possible,” says production supervisor and location manager Caleb Duffy. “We’re too identifiable. We’re an international city with too many iconic places to re-create anywhere else. The streets are different; the trees and foliage are different.” Nevertheless, this year, Russell Crowe is reportedly filming the L.A.-set thriller
Bear Country
in Queensland, Australia
.
As the labor of making movies and shows splinters across far-flung cities and countries, Hollywood has become dislodged from its physical home. Some of these new hubs may suit the needs of individual projects, but none of them offers what L.A. did for most of the past century: a stable gravitational center where crews can make a living and the craft can be passed down. data.title: Amelia Earhart's Reckless Final Flights
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）在尝试进行环球飞行时，在夏威夷的卢克机场发生坠机事故。她的飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员幸存。埃尔哈特计划成为首位完成环球飞行的女性，但她在起飞时忽视了经验丰富的飞行员保罗·曼兹（Paul Mantz）的建议，导致事故。尽管她早在1928年因成为首位跨大西洋飞行的女性而闻名，但她实际只是乘客。1932年，她独自驾驶单引擎飞机跨越大西洋，尽管条件恶劣且最终降落在爱尔兰的牧场。这次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。然而，成功将带来巨大的商业和媒体机会，NBC和CBS甚至争夺广播权。尽管有导航员陪同，埃尔哈特的准备和练习不足，更多时间花在了宣传和商业活动上。

不同观点：

• **[cylinder714]** 提供了关于Earhart飞行事故的技术细节，指出其缺乏无线电操作经验是悲剧的重要因素，并提到有人在飞行前拆除了关键的天线设备，认为这是不明智的举动。
• **[WalterBright]** 引用其父亲（一名B-17导航员和职业飞行员）的观点，认为Earhart是鲁莽的飞行员，表达了对其飞行技术的不满，但也表示对另一位女性飞行员Jacqueline Cochran的钦佩。
• **[Kon-Peki]** 提出Earhart被讨论为“鲁莽”主要因为她是女性且失败了，而其他同样失败的男性飞行员却没有受到同样关注，暗示性别因素在其中起到了作用。
• **[0xbadcafebee]** 认为Earhart这样的故事提醒人们两件事：历史创造者往往需要一些“疯狂”，以及无需掩饰英雄的缺陷，因为他们的传奇依然会流传下去。

• **历史背景**：[beedeebeedee] 强调了飞行早期阶段的普遍鲁莽性，并通过提到1920年代阿拉斯加的飞行员故事（如Eielson和Wilkins）来对比Earhart的情况，指出当时整个行业都在学习如何让飞行变得更安全。

• **语言问题**：[bauble] 对文章中使用“human navigators”代替“male navigators”表示困惑，认为这是不必要的或错误的措辞。

争议焦点：
• Earhart是否因其性别而被过度批评，以及她的飞行是否真的比同时代的其他飞行员更鲁莽。
• 关于Earhart飞行事故中的技术问题，特别是无线电和天线设备的准备是否充分。

Sparks flew, a wing bent, and the landing gear snapped off as the silver Lockheed Electra 10-E plane smashed into the runway at Luke Field, outside Honolulu. The pilot’s only stroke of luck was that the aircraft, which contained nearly a thousand gallons of fuel, didn’t explode.
The thirty-nine-year-old Amelia Earhart and her crew of two navigators, Fred Noonan and Harry Manning, crawled out of the wreckage, unsettled but otherwise unhurt. They had meant to depart on the second leg of a gruelling voyage: a round-the-world flight that had begun in Oakland, California, and would continue westward, with two dozen or so stops, before ending up back in Oakland. People close to Earhart knew that she wasn’t fully ready for a challenge of this magnitude, and so a work-around had been devised. An extra crew member with extensive flight experience, Paul Mantz, had joined the flight to Hawaii. On the runway in Oakland, he switched places with Earhart and assumed the throttles during takeoff. She then piloted most of the way to Oahu, but Mantz often took over.
As they approached Luke Field, Mantz sensed that Earhart had “pilot fatigue.” He asked her, “Do you want to land it?”
“No, you land it,” Earhart said.
He did so, then said farewell. Earhart had been able to observe Mantz’s handling of the plane over the Pacific, and from now on she would be the only pilot onboard. Flying the Electra solo wouldn’t be easy. Although the plane had state-of-the-art technology for its time, piloting it demanded constant coördination among the throttle, the rudder, and the control column—especially during takeoff and landing. While taking off on the second leg, Earhart ignored advice that Mantz had given her not to “jockey the throttles”—change the speed to maintain direction and balance—and the plane veered into a violent spin across the runway. The press had assembled to watch Earhart soar, and instead witnessed an embarrassment.
The stakes were huge. Men had been flying around the world since 1924, when a team of eight military officers completed a twenty-seven-thousand-mile journey in a hundred and seventy-five days (with seventy-four stops). Only one pilot had done a solo circumnavigation: a Texan named Wiley Post. In 1933, Post completed a fifteen-thousand-mile journey, traversing Germany, the Soviet Union, Alaska, and Canada. Four years later, a round-the-world flight remained daunting. Earhart planned to have human navigators on board with her, but she’d be the first female pilot to accomplish the feat.
Earhart had become instantly famous in 1928, as the first woman to cross the Atlantic in a plane. But, though she’d been photographed wearing a flight suit and a leather helmet, she was merely a passenger; the plane had actually been piloted by two men, Wilmer Stultz and Louis Gordon. She had since been working on establishing her command of the cockpit. There were plenty of accomplished female pilots who could’ve taken command of a transatlantic flight themselves, and some of these women considered Earhart’s notoriety unearned. In 1932, after logging more flight miles—but not as many as other top female pilots—she flew solo across the Atlantic in a cramped red Vega, a single-engine plane barely insulated against storms and cold temperatures. She fought exhaustion, iced wings, and a broken altimeter. Her intention was to land in Paris, but she ended up in a cow field in Ireland. Earhart approached the experience with an easy, almost reckless, confidence. She’d always been this way; as a girl growing up in the Kansas City area, she jury-rigged a “roller coaster” with steep ramps, then barrelled down it and fell off, only to exult, “This is just like flying!”
A globe-circling flight would be Earhart’s lengthiest journey by far, twenty-nine thousand miles hugging the equator. This wasn’t mere hopping among landmasses, as with Post’s route. Her path had been ambitiously charted to include a refuelling stop on Howland Island, a speck between Hawaii and Australia. A pilot making such a journey needed to be in excellent shape, with sufficient strength and stamina to manage the controls in turbulence, particularly during long hours in a cockpit with no autopilot. The dangers were extraordinary: enormous stretches over open ocean, unpredictable weather, extended isolation, intense psychological pressure. Yet the rewards promised to be substantial, from marketing opportunities to media attention. NBC and CBS were fighting over the rights to exclusive broadcasts.
Noonan and Manning had agreed to accompany Earhart nearly the whole way. They were excited to be associated with her glamour, but they also considered the job a risk. Rather than spending time practicing in the powerful Electra, Earhart had been crisscrossing the country, giving lectures, making sponsorship appearances, and attending promotional events. For a while, she had a gig as the aviation editor at
Cosmopolitan

• **[cylinder714]** 提供了关于Earhart飞行事故的技术细节，指出其缺乏无线电操作经验是悲剧的重要因素，并提到有人在飞行前拆除了关键的天线设备，认为这是不明智的举动。

• **[Kon-Peki]** 提出Earhart被讨论为“鲁莽”主要因为她是女性且失败了，而其他同样失败的男性飞行员却没有受到同样关注，暗示性别因素在其中起到了作用。
• **[0xbadcafebee]** 认为Earhart这样的故事提醒人们两件事：历史创造者往往需要一些“疯狂”，以及无需掩饰英雄的缺陷，因为他们的传奇依然会流传下去。

• **技术分析**：[a-r-t] 提供了Veritasium关于Earhart最后一次飞行的技术分析视频链接，深入探讨了飞行中的技术问题。
• **历史背景**：[beedeebeedee] 强调了飞行早期阶段的普遍鲁莽性，并通过提到1920年代阿拉斯加的飞行员故事（如Eielson和Wilkins）来对比Earhart的情况，指出当时整个行业都在学习如何让飞行变得更安全。
• **编辑风格批评**：[johnyzee] 对评论中使用变音符号（如"coördinated"）表示不满，认为这是不必要的矫饰。

• 关于Earhart飞行事故中的技术问题，特别是无线电和天线设备的准备是否充分。

data.title: American Science and Surplus is fighting for its life
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 美国科学与 surplus 商店成立于1937年，最初以销售 rejected 镜头和摄影设备起家，如今已发展成为销售实验室设备、军用剩余物资、工具、电子产品、玩具等各种商品的知名店铺。然而，这家拥有近90年历史的老店正面临生存危机，受疫情和成本上涨影响，生意艰难。为避免关闭，店铺发起了一项20万美元的众筹活动。这家位于芝加哥郊区的商店反映了本地零售业面临的挑战，受到大型零售商和电商巨头的冲击。店主Pat Meyer表示，银行不愿贷款，利率高企，他们只能向忠实顾客求助。尽管如此，这家店依旧凭借丰富的商品和独特的魅力吸引了众多顾客，许多人来这里寻找独特的物品。Meyer希望这家承载了几代人记忆的商店能够继续存活下去。

It was shortly after moving into Chicago's Jefferson Park neighborhood that I saw the sign for the first time: American Science & Surplus. My curiosity piqued, I pulled into the strip mall and walked into a store filled with an unimaginable variety of lab equipment, military surplus, tools, electronics, toys, and so much more.
Now, nearly 90 years after its launch selling "reject lenses" as American Lens & Photo,
American Science & Surplus
is facing an existential threat. The COVID-19 pandemic and increased costs hit the business hard, so the store has launched a
GoFundMe campaign looking to raise $200,000
from customers and fans alike. What's happening in suburban Chicago is a microcosm of the challenges facing local retail, with big-box retailers and online behemoths overwhelming beloved local institutions. It's a story that has played out countless times in the last two-plus decades, and owner Pat Meyer is hoping this tale has a different ending.
American Science & Surplus owner Pat Meyer holds the two most popular items in the store: $4 solenoid switches that are used to repair a well-known brand of single-cup coffee makers.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
American Science & Surplus owner Pat Meyer holds the two most popular items in the store: $4 solenoid switches that are used to repair a well-known brand of single-cup coffee makers.
Credit:
Eric Bangeman
Launching a fundraiser was a tough choice for Meyer. "I don't like asking people for money," he said.
With his voice catching, he continued: "It's hard for me to talk about sometimes, because the more I'm in the store, the more I see how much people care about it and don't want it to go away."
And the current environment is tough for small business owners. "Banks… are real hesitant [about lending] money," Meyer told Ars. "Interest rates are high, too. So we decided that we were going to try and reach out to the community that we built over the last 88 years."
Walk into any of the three American Science & Surplus' stores in the Illinois-Wisconsin area—two in Illinois, Park Ridge and Geneva, and one in Milwaukee—and it's easy to see why it has such a devoted following. Each aisle could be a store of its own. One has stationery and office supplies. Another has military surplus. The next one over has tools. I head over there regularly just to wander the aisles and see what's in stock. Other times I go looking for a particular oddball item—and I usually find it there.
A long history
Old catalogs from the American Lens & Photo days.
Credit:
American Science & Surplus
Old catalogs from the American Lens & Photo days.
Credit:
American Science & Surplus
American Science & Surplus got its start in 1937 and has expanded its inventory and reach ever since. And Meyer has been a part of the story for the last four decades. "I've done everything in the company that there is to do," he said. "I started off literally scraping floors and Windexing, driven our trucks. I've done warehouse sales, I've done tent sales. I've been store manager, assistant manager, I've done—there isn't anything in this company that I haven't—and it's been my life for 41 years."
Over time, the store has moved far beyond lenses and lab equipment. There's a science toy section and an aisle devoted to Etsy-style craft supplies. But other, once-thriving areas of the business have suffered. When I first discovered American Science & Surplus in the early 2000s, I would always linger at the massive telescope section. The store staff was always more than happy to answer my questions and explain the differences between the scopes. Now, telescopes are just a small corner of the store, and sales are infrequent. "People come in to ask questions and then buy the telescopes online," Meyer explained.
One of the display cases in the Park Ridge store.

My kids loved to search through the fossils and minerals when they were younger.

data.title: Destination: Jupiter
data.author: AndrewLiptak
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了人类对木星的探索和想象。1610年，伽利略首次通过望远镜观察到木星的四颗主要卫星，改变了对太阳系的理解。古代巴比伦、中国和希腊罗马的学者也曾对木星进行过观察和命名。16世纪，哥白尼提出日心说，随后开普勒和伽利略的观测进一步证实了这一理论。随着科学发展，木星成为文学作品中的热门目的地，18世纪伏尔泰的《微米伽斯》和19世纪晚期凡尔纳、威尔斯等作家的科幻小说都描绘了人类对木星及其卫星的想象和探索。文章还提到木星的科学特征，如其大气层和著名的大红斑，这些都是当时天文学家观察的重点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科幻与科学之间的相互影响，以及以木星及其卫星为背景的科幻作品

不同观点：
• [ednite] 认为科幻作家与科学家之间存在互相影响的关系。他提到自己的写作常常从当前科学可能引领我们走向何方开始，并提出未来的发展是由科幻中的愿景驱动，还是由实际的工程和科学实现推动，或者可能是两者无意间的结合。

• [zabzonk] 则从科学现实角度出发，指出在以木星为背景的科幻故事中存在科学上的不准确性。他提到由于木星强烈的磁场和致命辐射带，使得以人类为核心的故事难以在木星上展开。同时指出，前往木星系统的探测器必须经过严密的防护。

• [A_D_E_P_T] 补充了关于木星的最著名的科幻小说之一，亚瑟·克拉克的《与美杜莎相遇》，并提到该作品的影响力。他还提到斯蒂芬·巴克斯特和阿拉斯泰尔·雷诺兹为此书写的优秀续集《美杜莎编年史》。

• [bouncycastle] 从个人经验出发，提到木星和土星的卫星经常被用作主机名，并分享了自己在使用这些名称（如Callisto、Europa、Ganymede）时的技术设置情况。

• [arjunbajaj] 受到讨论启发，推荐了一本通过探索土星卫星Enceladus上的数据集来教授PostgreSQL的小说《Curious Moon》，并给出了购买链接。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科幻作品中科学准确性的问题。[zabzonk] 强调了科学现实对科幻创作的限制，而[ednite] 更关注科幻对科学未来发展的启发作用。

• 讨论中提到了具体的科幻作品及其影响力，如[A_D_E_P_T] 提到的《与美杜莎相遇》以及其续集《美杜莎编年史》。

• [bouncycastle] 和 [arjunbajaj] 的评论展示了科幻在技术文化中的实际应用，如主机名命名和技术教学小说。

整体来看，评论围绕科幻与科学的互动关系展开，既有对科学准确性的关注，也有对科幻启发作用的认可，同时还提到了具体作品和实际应用。
