Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
What’s next for LTO?
So one can expect LTO-11 to launch sometime in 2029. LTO’s latest roadmap goes up to LTO-14 with a native capacity of 576TB but this document will almost certainly be changed because of LTO-10’s unexpected (and disappointing) capacity change.
Symply, a storage hardware expert that launched the first LTO-9 tape drive, will start shipping LTO-10 products as early as mid-June 2025 from $11,995 (SAS) with devices equiped with other interfaces (Ethernet and Thunderbolt) costing more.
Symply told TechRadar Pro that they will provide pricing details for LTO-10 media soon. They also told us “the LTO-10 media is 1035m in length which is the same as LTO-9. It is a high density on the media that enable the higher capacity.”
LTO-9 is currently the cheapest of the LTO family, costing around $5 per TB; a 30TB tape would likely sell for more than $150.
IBM, one of the founders of LTO, has also announced an LTO 10 tape drive,
while Spectra Logic
announced support for the new media
.
25 years and still going strong
It’s been a quarter of a century already since LTO-1 hit the market and while it has many critics (
including within the US government
), its resilience, value for money and ability to adapt to countless storage demands makes it a reliable partner regardless of the use case.
We witnessed the demise of competitors (like

data.title: Precious Plastic is in trouble
data.author: diggan
data.article_summary: Precious Plastic，一个旨在全球推广塑料回收的开放资源项目，正面临生存危机。自2020年发布第四版以来，该项目通过与全球超过100名志愿者合作，开发了专业机器、工作坊启动包等，并在2023年实现了显著影响：1100个组织在56个国家回收了140万公斤塑料，创造了370万美元的收入。然而，项目面临三大问题：首先，因新冠疫情和建筑问题，团队失去了工作空间；其次，项目缺乏可持续的商业模式，无法在不与社区竞争的情况下产生足够收入；最后，团队遭遇法律诉讼，进一步加剧了财务困境。这些挑战使得项目难以为继，急需找到解决方案以继续推进使命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Precious Plastic组织的运营、透明度、未来方向以及其在塑料回收领域的实际作用和影响

不同观点：
• [ljm] 认为该组织虽然收到了大量捐款，但选择将资金用于社区项目而非解决组织内部问题。他质疑组织的领导层是否真正反思过错误，并担心捐款可能被用于不透明的用途，甚至可能是骗局。
• [krisoft] 指出Precious Plastic缺乏清晰的路线图，无法明确未来发展方向和资金用途，尤其是“版本5”相比“版本4”的具体改进和贡献不明确。他认为如果没有方向性说明，组织的确存在问题。
• [brikym] 认为依靠小规模的个人行动无法解决塑料污染问题，主张应集中力量迫使工业界承担责任。他批评Precious Plastic这样的项目反而可能让塑料生产显得更加可接受，违背了环保初衷。
• [kleton] 提出不同观点，认为塑料回收本质上会导致质量下降和微塑料产生，建议通过焚烧塑料产生能源，而不是试图重复利用低质量塑料。
• [nchmy] 对Precious Plastic感到失望，认为该组织在十年多的时间里没有建立可持续的商业模式。他批评组织删除了原有的论坛，并认为其葡萄牙的基地更像是一个“嬉皮公社”，而不是一个务实的项目。
• [monkmartinez] 从美国的角度出发，指出开设工作空间面临高昂的设备成本和获取塑料原材料的困难，尤其是在美国“回收”行业已经被大公司垄断的情况下。
• [decimalenough] 质疑Precious Plastic的机器是否真正具有独特性，指出市场上已有类似产品且价格更低，认为其开源模式的实际价值不明确。
• [mc007] 强烈批评Precious Plastic，称其为“欺诈性组织”，认为其设计和声明都缺乏证据支持，并提供了一份报告链接来支持其指控。

补充讨论：
• [papaver-somnamb] 建议Precious Plastic应缩小其职责范围，专注于其最擅长的领域，并将商业运营交给专业人士处理。他还指出塑料行业需要改革，并提到某些材料如玻璃和金属才是真正可回收的。
• [superzamp] 提到该帖已经发布六个月，质疑Precious Plastic目前的状态，尤其在其当时声称缺乏资金的情况下。
• [spoaceman7777] 认为文章像是在请求外界不要救助他们，批评其没有提出防止未来管理失误的具体计划，并建议他们寻求外界建议以避免继续浪费时间和金钱。
• [Scrapemist] 提到荷兰的工业回收设施因新塑料价格低廉而面临关闭或破产，指出立法强制生产者处理废物或对新塑料征税可能是解决之道，但认为强大的游说团体阻止了这一进程。
• [KnuthIsGod] 提到Precious Plastic卷入了一场长时间的诉讼，导致高昂的法律费用，进一步加剧了组织的问题。
• [meindnoch] 认为小规模的塑料回收项目只会产生低质量的塑料制品和微塑料，主张不应鼓励这种业余的回收方式。

争议焦点：
• Precious Plastic的透明度和资金使用是否合理。
• 组织是否真正有能力解决塑料污染问题，还是仅仅在制造更多的问题。
• 开源模式和其机器的实际价值是否如宣传所言。
• 领导层是否应该为过去的错误负责并下台。
• 塑料回收的实际可行性和是否应通过立法迫使工业界承担更多责任。

Precious Plastic

Hey world
This is a heavy message to send, but essential for the future of Precious Plastic. It will either make it or not. In this post Iâll give a detailed overview of all the current problems we have, how it got to this point and whats next. A short summarised video is below. No
need
to watch, it's all in the text.
â
Our last big development
â
Lets start with our last big development. Â 2020, when we released Version 4, this was our latest release. We worked about 1,5 year with over +100 people from around the world. We developed the first âProâ Machines, a Sheetpress, Starterkits, Business calculators, new moulds, products and more. Looking back this was quite a unique moment. A lot of passionate work was done by volunteers and everything was shared Open Source online for free. Here some of the things we made
With a relatively small amount of money, we reached a global impact in 2023 of over 1100 organzations in 56 countries, who recycled 1.400.000KG Plastic, they generated together a revenue of +$3.7 Million, employed 530 people, works with 3.405 volunteers and built 1.175 machines. (And this is only from the workspaces who shared their data last year) Learn more about our impact
here
.
â
âï¸This was the good part. Lets get into our problems
How we work
In order to understand our problems itâs important to know how Precious Plastic is developed since its unusual. We work in what we call Versions. Version 1 got released in 2013 and the latest one 4 years ago. The principle is, we develop a lot of new things, share them online for free. And then whoever was involved takes a holiday or goes off to something else. They really have to go because at that point we spend all our money. The workspace is empty, the work drops, nothing new is made, we wait. Up until now for some magical reason we always received a gift to continue moving forward. From winning awards, to getting a big workspace donated. Whenever we got enough resources we assembled a team and started developing again.. Each time the team and amount of work grew. Until the latest version, here the problems started.
When the Problems started
â
We worked in versions not because we wanted to, but because we had to. We share everything online for free because we believe recycling knowledge should be available for everyone. As a consequence we donât generate enough income to pay a team all year around. But after Version 4 a small group of seven dedicated ambitious volunteers wanted to try and sustain Precious Plastic all year around. So we can continue development and have a bigger impact to reduce plastic waste. This by itself is a hard job but we also had some extra problems on the way
â
#1 No workspace
â
The team was ready to continue work. But just a few weeks later Covid-19 came to the world, but this wasnât our main problem. Our problem was Chrome-6, a chemical the municipality found in the paint from the building that was applied 40 years ago. Which meant we had to leave the workspace fast, and the building was large, we had a lot of machines and items to sell, in a short amount of time, during lockdowns. This meant we had to sell many things below value since that period most people were looking to buy bread machines, not robot arms. After the exhausting/rushed job of leaving our workspace we could stay in the garage/shed in the house of one of the team members in France. It was nice we had a base to continue, but it was much smaller and temporary. It was quite a downgrade.
#2 No business model
â
One of the main goals of this small team was trying to find a business model that would serve Precious Plasticâs mission, bring income to sustain a team and not compete with the rest of the community. The last one is difficult, because our most logical and common model would be to sell machines and moulds. There are not many Open Source Hardware projects like Precious Plastic in the world. And the ones that exist mostly sell their products. Arduino sells their circuit boards, Prusa sells 3d printers. However in our case weâre also building a global network of machine builders that can provide local recycling equipment. We didn't want to compete with our own community.
The plan was to do Projects or as we called them, Collabs. It meant to help others set up their projects. Sort of a consultancy. The team setup quite a few cool projects, from a refugee camp in a desert in Algeria to a big Sheetpress in Nigeria. And meanwhile released a few new machine drawings. The model somewhat worked, we continued development and could do meaningful work. However it was financially always tight and often didnât bring in enough money to sustain the team (that was getting paid minimum Dutch wage). But what really broke it was the next problem
â
#3 Lawsuit
â

data.title: Japan's births in 2024 fall below 700k for first time
data.author: ivewonyoung
data.article_summary: 2024年，日本的新生儿数量首次降至70万以下，为686,061人，同比减少5.7%。总生育率也创下历史新低，降至1.15。这一趋势已持续九年，且下降速度比政府预期提前15年。虽然结婚数量在2024年有所增加，但死亡人数达到1,605,298人，创战后新高，自然减少人数为919,237人。东京生育率最低，为0.96，而冲绳最高，为1.54。专家原预计2039年出生数才会降至68万范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本战后死亡人数和人口自然减少的问题

不同观点：
• [duxup] 引用了数据，指出日本报告的死亡人数为1,605,298，是战后时期最高的，同时人口自然减少（死亡人数减去出生人数）达到了创纪录的919,237，连续18年人口呈现下降趋势。这表明日本正面临严重的人口减少问题，且趋势明显。

• [mensetmanusman] 对此数据的未来影响进行了调侃，提出通过在当前数字上“增加两个零并减去15%”来估算一个人死亡时的总人口。这暗示对未来人口大幅减少的担忧，并可能认为当前的趋势将持续并加剧。

补充讨论：
- [duxup] 的数据引用表明了日本当前人口问题的严峻性，重点在于死亡人数和出生人数之间的巨大差距。
- [mensetmanusman] 的评论则带有一种悲观预测的色彩，通过一种假设性的计算方式表达了对未来人口下降趋势的看法。
- 争议的焦点可能在于如何有效应对这种人口减少的趋势，以及对未来人口估算的准确性和潜在社会经济影响的讨论。

44187325.article_content:
This unrelated photo shows a newborn at a clinic in Otsu, Shiga Prefecture, in June 11, 2022. (Mainichi)
TOKYO (Kyodo) -- The number of births in Japan fell below 700,000 for the first time in 2024, declining 5.7 percent from the previous year to 686,061, government data showed Wednesday, highlighting a continued trend of delayed marriages and childbirths.
Japan's total fertility rate -- the average number of children a woman is estimated to bear in her lifetime -- also fell to a record-low 1.15, down from 1.20 in 2023, according to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare.
Both the number of births and the fertility rate have decreased for nine consecutive years. The pace of Japan's declining birthrate is now 15 years ahead of government projections.
The full-year figures exclude babies born to foreign nationals.
The number of marriages, a key factor influencing future birth trends, increased for the first time in two years in 2024 to 485,063, up by 10,322 from a year earlier.
A total of 1,605,298 deaths were reported, the highest number in the postwar period, while the natural decrease -- deaths minus births -- reaching a record 919,237, marking a decline for the 18th straight year.
Japan's birthrate has been falling since hitting a peak during the second baby boom in 1973, when around 2.09 million births were recorded. The figure fell below 1 million in 2016 and below 800,000 in 2022.
The National Institute of Population and Social Security Research had not projected births to drop into the 680,000 range until 2039.
By prefecture, Tokyo recorded the lowest fertility rate at 0.96, followed by Miyagi at 1.00 and Hokkaido at 1.01. Okinawa in southern Japan had the highest rate at 1.54, followed by Fukui at 1.46.

data.title: Bookish Diversions: Reading as Help for Living

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过阅读小说来帮助处理复杂生活决策的观点。作者Joel J. Miller引用了Steven Johnson的《Farsighted》一书，指出小说如乔治·艾略特的《 Middlemarch 》可以帮助读者练习应对多维度和多层次的决策。小说不仅提供了对潜在事件的模拟，还通过角色的内心活动让读者更好地理解人类情感和认知。这不仅有助于自我反思，还能为现实生活中的决策提供智慧。此外，作者还提到，阅读经典小说如《Jane Eyre》、《Anna Karenina》等，可以提升对智力卓越性的欣赏，尽管对提升个人道德的直接作用存疑。总的来说，小说作为一种自我反思的工具，能够帮助读者更好地理解自己和周围世界。

¶ Decisions, decisions!
Steven Johnson
’s 2018 book
Farsighted
presents a method for processing decisions—not the easy kind (cherry pie or apple?) but the tough,
Russ Roberts
–y,
wild
kind, with all the considerations and contingencies that spool out like thirty-seven balls of yarn rolling downhill. Do I:
marry Sally?
put Dad in the nursing home?
change a policy that affects my coworkers’ retirement?
move to Montreal?
chuck it all and go into the car-wash business with my cousin Earl?
Good luck!
Photo by
Letizia Bordoni
on
Unsplash
Wild problems often involve simple, binary choices—yes or no—but they contain countless concerns and consequences. Sally, Dad, coworkers, Montreal, Earl: to one degree or another, the variables multiple as we consider them and ramify in ways we can’t fully corral.
To decide, says Johnson, we must manage to map the variables and then predict the outcomes. We’ll do so imperfectly, and we’ll get more wrong than right—whether the extent of our errors proves material or not. (The future ain’t easy, friends.)
One help in this fraught and feeble process? Surprisingly, Johnson suggests novels, pointing to George Eliot’s
Middlemarch
as his primary example. The tortured decisions with which Dorothea and Lydgate contend involve multiple dimensions and layers, and Eliot takes us inside their minds as they messily try mapping the variables and predicting their outcomes. Novels are for their readers, in other words, practice. “When we read those novels,” says Johnson, “we are not just entertaining ourselves; we are also rehearsing for our own real-world experiences.”
But the practice extends beyond personal considerations.
What’s the Big Deal about ‘Middlemarch’?
Joel J Miller
·
November 20, 2024
Read full story
¶ Thinking across dimensions.
I recently returned to Johnson’s
Farsighted
because Johnson did. In
an essay here at Substack
he mentioned
reading a tweet
in which Stripe CEO Patrick Collison recounted the experience of reading ten classic novels during the year:
Jane Eyre
by Charlotte Brontë
Middlemarch
by George Eliot
To the Lighthouse
by Virginia Woolf
Bleak House
by Charles Dickens
Portrait of a Lady
by Henry James
Anna Karenina
by Leo Tolstoy
Life and Fate
by Vasily Grossman
Heart of Darkness
by Joseph Conrad
Madame Bovary
by Gustave Flaubert
The Magic Mountain
by Thomas Mann
Why would a Silicon Valley tech exec read these sorts of books? Collison admits skepticism about fiction’s power to improve our personal morality but says they can elevate our appreciation of intellectual excellence.
What about improving our understanding of human nature more broadly? “There is almost certainly some extent to which this argument is valid,” says Collison, “though I always wonder: do they help you better understand
humanity
, or better understand
the kind of people who write books like these
?”
I don’t know if novels help us better understand abstract humanity. But I’m convinced as theaters for self-reflection they do help us better understand ourselves and what we think about the world around us; that might generalize to the whole species, but it needn’t do so to be valuable for the individual reader.
Revisiting his argument in
Farsighted
, Johnson offers two explanations of why, one more obvious, the other less so. First, the obvious one:
Novels (and fictional narratives in general) [are] extensions of the human mind’s marvelous aptitude for building
simulations
of potential events. It’s something we do so effortlessly that we rarely stop to think about how nuanced a skill it really is: creatively projecting forward into our possible futures based on our previous experience of the world. Narratives of all sorts allow you to parachute into other simulated experiences, which ultimately give you more data for your own simulations. But novels, I would argue, give you the richest simulation of the
interior life
of other people’s experiences: you get a ringside view of all that emotional and cognitive action. . . . It seems fairly obvious to me that there is practical utility in running these simulations. We accumulate wisdom that we can apply to our own lives by watching other people live theirs.
But, says Johnson, great novelists can push us further, past the mere interiority of their characters’ mental and emotional experience. They can take us across the many dimensions a character’s thought process might travel, all of the external pressures and factors that could come to bear.

data.author: bitsavers
data.article_summary:
2008年，当时仍是民主党员的唐纳德·特朗普期间，一位匿名博主Mencius Moldbug发表了一份名为“致思想开放的进步人士的公开信”的宣言。他批评平等主义是世界问题的根源，并指责媒体和学术界维持左派自由主义共识（他称之为“大教堂”）。他主张摧毁现有社会秩序，终止民主、宪法和法治，将权力移交给类似CEO的人物，如史蒂夫·乔布斯或马克·安德森，将政府转变为高度武装、超盈利的公司。该政权将出售公立学校、摧毁大学、废除媒体、监禁“未文明化的人群”，并大规模解雇公务员和中断国际关系。

Moldbug自称为保皇党，支持君主制，反对英国和美国的革命。他的思想吸引了一些科技人士和理性主义者，形成了“新反动运动”或“黑暗启蒙”，影响了后来的另类右翼。2013年，Moldbug被揭露为旧金山程序员Curtis Yarvin，他同时创立了公司Tlon，投资者包括Peter Thiel和Andreessen Horowitz。尽管其思想引发争议，但在特朗普时代，其强人统治观念得到了呼应。

不同观点：
• eikenberry认为Yarvin的观点可以简化为“一个仁慈且有能力的独裁者是最好的政府形式”，但指出找到这样一个理想人物是不现实的，历史上没有可靠的系统能实现这一点。
• legitster提到自己曾批评Orson Scott Card作品中孩子通过网络言论上台的设定不现实，但现在认为这种现象可能正在成为现实。
• rubyfan质疑为何主流媒体突然开始报道Yarvin的想法，暗示可能有其他动机。
• A_D_E_P_T将Yarvin的观点视为社会压力和复杂问题积累的结果，认为其表现是社会“燃烧殆尽”的征兆，并指出Yarvin的观点只是其中一种表现。

• defen询问是否有办法找到最早讨论Yarvin观点的帖子，以了解当时人们的反应。
• senkora提到Scott Alexander对Yarvin近期行为的评论，认为Yarvin的旧作解释了为何其新作是无稽之谈。
• skrebbel表示不理解Yarvin为何获得如此多关注。
• ivraatiems认为Yarvin的意识形态源自于掩盖自我弱点的傲慢，并指出其作品和公司Urbit都显示出过度复杂和不实用的特点。
• mmustapic质疑Yarvin将CEO比作反民主的独裁者的观点，认为这在民主社会中不应被接受。
• esseph对讨论内容表示反感并建议删除，认为如果不想看可以不看。
• exizt88指出Yarvin的一个主要观点（过去每一代都比现在更右翼）很容易被反驳，并举出多个历史例子。
• rukuu001引用Yarvin关于“愚蠢”的定义，强调其指的是缺乏社会责任感。
• arp242批评Yarvin关于合法性、问责制和继承问题的解决方案过于天真和简单化，并指出其自认为最聪明的心理可能导致其持有一些非常偏颇的观点。

补充讨论：
• Yarvin的观点被多方质疑，尤其是其可行性和历史依据。
• 讨论中多次提到Yarvin的傲慢和自认为最聪明的态度，认为这是其观点偏颇的原因之一。
• 主流媒体对Yarvin观点的关注引发了质疑，有人认为这是社会问题积累的结果。
• 一些评论者对Yarvin的追随者及其意识形态的影响表示担忧，认为这是一个 cautionary tale。

In the spring and summer of 2008, when
Donald Trump
was still a registered Democrat, an anonymous blogger known as Mencius Moldbug posted a serial manifesto under the heading “An Open Letter to Open-Minded Progressives.” Written with the sneering disaffection of an ex-believer, the hundred-and-twenty-thousand-word letter argued that egalitarianism, far from improving the world, was actually responsible for most of its ills. That his bien-pensant readers thought otherwise, Moldbug contended, was due to the influence of the media and the academy, which worked together, however unwittingly, to perpetuate a left-liberal consensus. To this nefarious alliance he gave the name the Cathedral. Moldbug called for nothing less than its destruction and a total “reboot” of the social order. He proposed “the liquidation of democracy, the Constitution, and the rule of law,” and the eventual transfer of power to a C.E.O.-in-chief (someone like Steve Jobs or Marc Andreessen, he suggested), who would transform the government into “a heavily-armed, ultra-profitable corporation.” This new regime would sell off public schools, destroy universities, abolish the press, and imprison “decivilized populations.” It would also fire civil servants en masse (a policy Moldbug later called
RAGE
—Retire All Government Employees) and discontinue international relations, including “security guarantees, foreign aid, and mass immigration.”
Moldbug acknowledged that his vision depended on the sanity of his chief executive: “Clearly, if he or she turns out to be Hitler or Stalin, we have just recreated Nazism or Stalinism.” Yet he dismissed the failures of twentieth-century dictators, whom he saw as too reliant on popular support. For Moldbug, any system that sought legitimacy in the passions of the mob was doomed to instability. Though critics labelled him a techno-fascist, he preferred to call himself a royalist or a Jacobite—a nod to partisans of James II and his descendants, who, in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, opposed Britain’s parliamentary system and upheld the divine right of kings. Never mind the French Revolution, the bête noire of reactionary thinkers: Moldbug believed that the English and American Revolutions had gone too far.
If Moldbug’s “Open Letter” showed little affection for the masses, it intimated that they might still have a use. “Communism was not overthrown by
Andrei Sakharov
,
Joseph Brodsky
, and
Václav Havel
,” he wrote. “What was needed was the combination of philosopher and crowd.” The best place to recruit this crowd, he said, was on the internet—a shrewd intuition. Before long, links to Moldbug’s blog, “Unqualified Reservations,” were being passed around by libertarian techies, disgruntled bureaucrats, and self-styled rationalists—many of whom formed the shock troops of an online intellectual movement that came to be known as neo-reaction, or the Dark Enlightenment. While few turned into outright monarchists, their contempt for Obama-era uplift seemed to find voice in Moldbug’s heresies. In his most influential coinage, which quickly gained currency among the nascent alt-right, Moldbug urged his readers to rouse themselves from their ideological slumber by taking the “red pill,” like Keanu Reeves’s character in “The Matrix,” who chooses daunting truth over contented ignorance.
In 2013, an article on the news site
TechCrunch
, titled “Geeks for Monarchy,” revealed that Mencius Moldbug was the cyber alias of a forty-year-old programmer in San Francisco named Curtis Yarvin. At the same time that he was trying to redesign the U.S. government, Yarvin was also dreaming up a new computer operating system that he hoped would serve as a “digital republic.” He founded a company that he named Tlon, for the
Borges
story “Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius,” in which a secret society describes an elaborate parallel world that begins to overtake reality. As he raised money for his startup, Yarvin became a kind of Machiavelli to his big-tech benefactors, who shared his view that the world would be better off if they were in charge. Tlon’s investors included the venture-capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund, the latter of which was started by the billionaire
Peter Thiel
. Both Thiel and Balaji Srinivasan, then a general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, had become friends with Yarvin after reading his blog, though e-mails shared with me revealed that neither was thrilled to be publicly associated with him at the time. “How dangerous is it that we are being linked?” Thiel wrote to Yarvin in 2014. “One reassuring thought: one of our hidden advantages is that these people”—social-justice warriors—“wouldn’t believe in a conspiracy if it hit them over the head (this is perhaps the best measure of the decline of the Left). Linkages make them sound really crazy, and they kinda know it.”

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新西兰土地价值税（LVT）的实施及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• gardnr认为新西兰实施土地价值税有约100年的历史，并分享了一份学术论文链接，暗示该文献可以为讨论提供有价值的信息。他似乎对LVT持较为支持的态度，认为其有历史实践基础。

• Aurornis指出，单纯依赖土地价值税（LVT）可能会导致税收负担不公平地转移。具体来说，拥有价值较低房屋的人税收负担会增加，而拥有高价值房屋的人税收负担会减少。他强调，单独对土地征税而忽视房屋价值，可能导致税收体系的累进性减弱，即拥有较便宜房屋的人（可能经济状况较差）会受到负面影响。

补充讨论：
• Aurornis进一步分析了土地和房屋分别征税的优点，认为分别征税可以确保拥有更昂贵房屋的人支付更多税款，从而体现税收的公平性和累进性。他担心，转向纯粹的土地价值税会忽视房屋价值对税收公平性的影响。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于土地价值税的公平性和累进性。Aurornis认为纯粹的土地价值税可能会导致税收负担不公平地转移，尤其是对经济状况较差的人不利，而gardnr似乎更关注LVT的历史实践和潜在优势。

总结：
主要讨论围绕土地价值税的实施效果展开，焦点在于其对不同经济状况人群的税收负担影响以及税收体系的公平性和累进性。Aurornis对纯粹的土地价值税持保留态度，强调需要考虑房屋价值以保持税收的公平性，而gardnr则通过分享文献来支持LVT的可行性和历史基础。

44188204.article_content:
Engineer Fixes and Re-Installs Old Payphones, Provides Free Calls to the Public
Patrick Schlott's RandTel
By
Rain Noe
-
June 4
in
Object Culture
Payphones "were the only things that were built to last for decades and be out in the elements," says electrical engineer Patrick Schlott. He should know; as a hobby, he buys secondhand payphones, rewires them, then asks local businesses in rural Vermont if they'd let him install them. His goal is to offer, for free, public telephone service. (Schlott foots the bill himself.)
"It's assumed most folks own cell phones," writes Schlott. "Well, not everyone does, sometimes they don't work out on dirt roads, sometimes you forget your charger, and sometimes you just really need to make a phone call. We aim to provide a valuable public service to the community while teaching people about the US telephone system that has over a century of history behind it."
Schlott's company,
RandTel
, currently operates three phones in his neck of Vermont: One at the North Tunbridge General Store in Tunbridge, one at the Latham Library and a third—a rotary model from the 1950s--at the town of Randolph's information booth. He's particularly proud of that last one, as "This installation is 100% solar-powered, provided graciously by Catamount Solar," he writes. "Many thanks to the White River Valley Chamber of Commerce for hosting!"

data.title: Differences in link hallucination and source comprehension across different LLM
data.author: hveksr
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的推理能力、事实核查能力以及链接和信息真实性的问题

不同观点：
• SubiculumCode认为，测试时的计算资源对文档理解有重要影响。低计算设置可能导致模型误解文本，而推理模型可以通过多次猜测和考虑多个目标来纠正错误。他还指出，Gemini 2.5的幻觉/虚构率最低，但对博客中的结果表示惊讶。他发现，当限制搜索来源（如仅限pubmed）并直接提供来源链接时，幻觉和输出质量有所改善。

• motorest引用了博客内容，批评LLMs在找不到和验证相关链接的情况下仍然坚持错误的输出，甚至虚构不存在的URL。他认为，要谈论博士级别的智能，LLMs必须能够进行博士级别的上下文寻找和信息验证，而不仅仅生成流畅的文本。

• simonw指出，o3和Claude 4在事实核查和利用搜索及网络工具方面远超GPT 4.1和Gemini 2.5。这些模型能够运行工具（如搜索工具）作为其“推理”阶段的一部分，这是一个令人兴奋的进展。

• dedicate强调，问题不仅在于模型弄错链接，还在于它们完全虚构链接并坚持错误。这种感觉与人类犯错不同，更像是一种欺骗行为。

• zone411提供了一个基准测试链接，用于比较LLMs基于提供文本虚构答案的频率，并表示结果可能与其他基准不同。

• milleramp提到对SIFT工具箱的理解误差，澄清它不是Scale-Invariant Feature Transform工具箱。

• eviks认为，讨论LLMs的“博士级别智能”是因为这些工具被定位为研究助手，帮助学生研究并得出自己的结论，即使它们在链接验证方面存在问题。

• dr_kiszonka指出，问题起始词（如"What"和"Did"）对答案质量有影响。

• diego_moita观察到，原创洞见和幻觉可能相关。o3模型在坚持错误和虚构解释方面表现得最有说服力，但也提供了最多的有趣洞见，这可能暗示某种深层真理或者仅仅是自我幻觉。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLMs在事实核查和链接验证方面的能力不足，尤其是它们虚构信息并坚持错误输出的倾向。
• 不同模型（如o3、Claude 4、Gemini 2.5）在处理信息真实性和推理能力上的表现差异是一个重要讨论点。
• 有人认为限制搜索来源可以改善输出质量，这提示了模型设计和数据来源选择的重要性。

44187336.article_content:
Is this the end or the beginning?
MeTooSlow
Jun 4, 2025
169
8,816
views
English (US)
Chess Personalities
Over the board
Chess
I never thought I’d be writing this. But here we are—Magnus Carlsen, the undisputed king of modern chess, just hinted that he might walk away from classical chess for good. And honestly? It feels like the end of an era. Or maybe the beginning of a new one.
Let’s be clear: Magnus didn’t make some dramatic, final-announcement speech. But after his recent loss to 19-year-old World Champion and Indian prodigy D Gukesh at Norway Chess, he made a few comments that hit hard. “I simply don’t enjoy classical chess anymore,” he said. Those words cut deep, not because I blame him, but because it says so much about where the game is right now.
If you’ve been following Magnus for years like I have, you know he’s never been one to chase titles for the sake of it. He already gave up the world championship title because the preparation grind wasn’t worth the stress. And now, it seems even elite round-robin events don’t bring him joy anymore. It’s not about losing (he’s done that before and bounced back), it’s about the
why
behind showing up to play.
And maybe that’s the most relatable thing about him.
Classical Chess Is a Grind
Let’s face it: classical chess at the top level is brutal. Hours of prep, memorizing 20+ move theory trees, and then sitting for 6-hour games that often end in razor-thin draws. Even watching it sometimes feels like homework. Sure, there's beauty in it, but when the top player in the world starts feeling like it’s a chore, maybe it’s time to listen.
The irony is that the guy who dominated the classical scene for over a decade may have helped push it to its current limits. Everyone caught up, databases exploded, and engines trained on neural nets started leveling the playing field. Now even super-GMs can’t just "outplay" people over the board without some insane prep.
Magnus Isn’t Done with Chess—Not Even Close
What’s clear is that Magnus isn’t quitting chess. He still thrives in rapid, blitz, bullet. And let’s be honest, he’s still the boss on Lichess when he logs on as DrNykterstein. He’s also been pushing formats like Freestyle Chess, where theory goes out the window and creativity takes center stage. That’s where you can see his love for the game again.
It reminds me of when I switch from grinding 30+0 to playing ultrabullet just for laughs. It’s still chess, but it
feels
different. More fun. More human.
Is This a Problem—or Just Evolution?
Some people are already sounding alarms: “If Magnus quits classical, who’s going to carry the torch?” But maybe we’re asking the wrong question. Maybe it’s time to ask what chess
needs
to stay meaningful and inspiring, not just for players, but for fans.
Does it need fewer draws? More hybrid formats? Shorter time controls? Randomized openings? I don’t have the answers, but I think we’re heading into a period where the chess world will have to decide what really matters: tradition, or innovation?
A Personal Goodbye (If This Is It)
If this really is Magnus’s slow farewell to classical chess, I just want to say thanks. Thanks for the games, the grind, the weird faces during deep thought, the immaculate endgames, and the way he made it look effortless—when we all knew it wasn’t.
Whether he’s dominating a 3-minute arena on Lichess or showing up at a chess960 showdown in Vegas, he’ll still be the GOAT in my eyes.

data.title: End of an Era: Landsat 7 Decommissioned After 25 Years of Earth Observation
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: Landsat 7卫星在运行25年后，于2025年6月4日正式退役。自1999年发射以来，它为地球观测做出了重要贡献，拍摄了大量关于地球地表变化的图像，涵盖了拉斯维加斯城市扩展、湖泊和植被变化等。尽管Landsat 7退役，Landsat 8和9仍在继续每八天提供一次完整的地球图像。Landsat 7的影像数据将保存在美国地质调查局（USGS），支持科学研究和自然资源管理。其传感器捕捉了9/11后、卡特里娜飓风和深水地平线漏油等事件的高分辨率图像，并参与了南极洲影像拼接等项目。退役后，Landsat 7将缓慢脱离轨道，约55年后重返地球大气层。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Landsat卫星项目及其相关科技基础设施的贡献、技术细节及未来发展

不同观点：
• jvanderbot认为，Landsat项目以及其他类似项目（如NOAA天气数据、GPS等）为社会提供了巨大的公共利益，且数据基本上是免费开放的。这些项目体现了为人类共同利益所做出的努力，但目前可能因为资金等问题处于不确定的状态。
  
• pqdbr对Landsat 7卫星在退役后需要55年才能重返大气层表示不解，并质疑为何不通过降低轨道使其立即坠毁。他引用了文章中的技术细节，但认为直接销毁可能更有效。

• wewewedxfgdf关心这些卫星在退役后是否还能继续工作，或者是否需要持续的人工干预。这涉及到卫星在无人维护的情况下是否还能自主运行和传输数据。

• mceoin提出了一个更长远的视角，认为地球观测技术的发展将使人类能够以高清视频的形式回顾地球历史，形成一个可以随时间滚动的地球全景记录。

• Animats指出Landsat 8和9仍在运行，因此Landsat 7的退役不会影响整体观测能力，并表示对气候变化观测计划可能被削减的担忧。

• perihelions反驳了关于Landsat Next的计划，声称该计划在特朗普政府期间被取消，并引用了相关预算文件和科学文章作为证据，指出多个地球观测卫星项目因政治原因被终止。

补充讨论：
• gnabgib提供了一个相关讨论的链接，指向另一个关于Landsat 7结束任务的新闻，显示出该话题在不同平台上的延续性。

• wffurr则提到Landsat影像在影视作品中的应用，如电影《金刚：骷髅岛》，显示出这些数据在娱乐产业中的价值。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于Landsat Next及其他地球观测卫星项目是否真的因政治原因被取消，以及这些项目未来的命运如何。perihelions引用的资料与主流报道形成对比，突显出信息来源的冲突和不确定性。

44188248.article_content:
End of an Era: Landsat 7 Decommissioned After 25 Years of Earth Observation
By
Communications and Publishing
June 4, 2025
After 25 years of capturing Earth's changing landscape, the Landsat 7 satellite received its final transmission from the U.S. Geological Survey and was officially decommissioned June 4, closing a remarkable chapter in space-based observation.
Show only left
Show only right
Sources/Usage: Public Domain.
View Media Details
Download Images
These Landsat 7 images showcase the first and last captures of the Las Vegas area, taken on July 4, 1999, and May 28, 2024, respectively. The images highlight the city, the surrounding desert landscape, and Lake Mead, using shortwave infrared (SWIR), near-infrared (NIR), and red bands to emphasize differences in vegetation, water, and urban growth. The final image, marking the satellite’s 25th anniversary, stands as a tribute to Landsat 7's quarter-century legacy of Earth observation.
While Landsat 7’s long watch over Earth comes to an end, Landsat 8, launched in 2013, and Landsat 9, launched in 2020, continue to work together to create a complete snapshot of Earth every eight days. Their successor—Landsat Next—is currently planned to launch in the early 2030s and provide even greater coverage and detail.
Launched in 1999 as a joint mission of the USGS and NASA, Landsat 7 significantly enhanced Earth observations and provided a key part of the Landsat program’s five decade-plus record of imaging the planet’s surface. The satellite's imagery will remain
archived
at the USGS Earth Resources Observation and Science Center, continuing to support scientific discovery and decision-making for the future.
“The Landsat satellites have delivered over 50 years of extraordinary science data, economic value and national security benefits by informing decisions in every sector of the economy—from monitoring drought in the West to guiding disaster recovery,” said
Sarah Ryker, USGS Acting Director
. “For 25 of those years, Landsat 7’s data helped farmers, land managers, city planners, and scientists, as well as communities around the world better understand and manage land, water, and other natural resources.”
Landsat 7 achieved many milestones over its 25 years of operation and was the first Landsat to downlink data to the newly established USGS ground station in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. It was also the first Landsat satellite to be fully operated 24/7 by the USGS after being launched by NASA.
Its Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus sensor delivered improved high-resolution imagery that expanded its capabilities, capturing critical historical events such as the aftermath of 9/11, Hurricane Katrina, and the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. The satellite also contributed to important projects, including the
Landsat Image Mosaic of Antarctica
, and inspired the "
Earth As Art
" collection, showcasing stunning visuals of the planet.
After ending its official mission in 2024, the USGS prepared Landsat 7 for decommissioning to follow responsible space practices and U.S. policies on keeping space clear of debris. The final steps included carefully lowering the satellite's orbit to decrease the risk of collisions and ensuring that all energy sources, such as fuel and batteries, are depleted to prevent the satellite from accidentally turning back on or creating debris. As Landsat 7 begins this decommissioned phase, it will drift silently in orbit for about 55 years before reentering Earth’s atmosphere.
To learn more about Landsat 7’s distinguished mission, visit:
A Final Farewell to Landsat 7 | U.S. Geological Survey
.

data.title: Endangered classic Mac plastic color returns as 3D-printer filament
data.author: CobaltFire
data.article_summary: 经典电脑收藏家Joe Strosnider推出了名为"Retro Platinum"的3D打印 filament，重现1980年代至1990年代苹果Macintosh电脑的标志性外观颜色。这种PLA filament可让爱好者打印怀旧物品、替换部件和配件，解决 vintage computing 社区中难以找到合适颜色材料的问题。该filament由Polar Filament生产，售价为每公斤21.99美元，适用于标准3D打印机，并兼容一些新打印机的自动材料系统。这一开发 coincides 随着3D打印复古电脑外壳和配件的兴趣增长，如SE Mini桌面外壳项目。Strosnider通过公开配方，让更多人能使用这种颜色，延续对经典苹果电脑的欣赏。

On Tuesday, classic computer collector Joe Strosnider
announced
the availability of a new 3D-printer filament that replicates the iconic "
Platinum
" color scheme used in classic Macintosh computers from the late 1980s through the 1990s. The PLA filament (PLA is short for polylactic acid) allows hobbyists to 3D-print nostalgic novelties, replacement parts, and accessories that match the original color of vintage Apple computers.
Hobbyists commonly feed this type of filament into
commercial desktop 3D printers
, which heat the plastic and extrude it in a computer-controlled way to fabricate new plastic parts.
The Platinum color, which Apple used in its desktop and portable computer lines starting with the
Apple IIgs
in 1986, has become synonymous with a distinctive era of classic Macintosh aesthetic. Over time, original Macintosh plastics have become
brittle and discolored
with age, so matching the "original" color can be a somewhat challenging and subjective experience.
A close-up of "Retro Platinum" PLA filament by Polar Filament.
Credit:
Polar Filament
Strosnider, who
runs a website
about his extensive vintage computer collection in Ohio, worked for years to color-match the distinctive beige-gray hue of the Macintosh Platinum scheme, resulting in a spool of hobby-ready plastic by Polar Filament and priced at
$21.99 per kilogram
.
According to a forum post, Strosnider paid approximately $900 to develop the color and purchase an initial 25-kilogram supply of the filament. Rather than keeping the formulation proprietary, he arranged for Polar Filament to make the color publicly available.
"I paid them a fee to color match the speaker box from inside my Mac Color Classic," Strosnider
wrote
in a Tinkerdifferent forum post on Tuesday. "In exchange, I asked them to release the color to the public so anyone can use it."
A spool of "Retro Platinum" PLA filament by Polar Filament.
Credit:
Polar Filament
The development addresses a gap in the
vintage computing
community, where enthusiasts sometimes struggle to find appropriately colored materials for restoration projects and new accessories. The new filament is an attempt to replace previous options that were either expensive, required international shipping, or had consistency issues that Strosnider described as "chalky."
The 1.75 mm filament works with standard 3D printers and is compatible with automated material systems used in some newer printer models. On Bluesky, Strosnider encouraged buyers to "order plenty, and let them know you want them to print it forever" to ensure continued production of the specialty color.
Extruded nostalgia
The timing of the filament's release coincides with growing interest in 3D-printed cases and accessories for vintage computer hardware. One example is the
SE Mini desktop case
, a project by "GutBomb" that transforms
Macintosh SE
and
SE/30
logic boards into compact desktop computers that can connect to modern displays. The case, designed to be 3D-printed in multiple pieces and assembled, represents the type of project that benefits from color-accurate filament.
A 3D-printed "SE Mini" desktop case that allows using a vintage compact Mac board in a new enclosure.
Credit:
Joe Strosnider
The SE Mini case requires approximately half a spool of filament and takes a couple of days to print on consumer 3D printers. Users can outfit the case with modern components, such as
Pico PSUs
and
BlueSCSI
storage devices, while maintaining the classic Macintosh appearance.
Why create new "retro" devices? Because it's fun, and it's a great way to merge technology's past with the benefits of recent tech developments. Projects like the Platinum PLA filament, the SE Mini case, and the dedication of hobbyists like Strosnider ensure that appreciation for Apple's computers of yore will continue for decades.
Benj Edwards
Senior AI Reporter
Benj Edwards
Senior AI Reporter
Benj Edwards is Ars Technica's Senior AI Reporter and founder of the site's dedicated AI beat in 2022. He's also a tech historian with almost two decades of experience. In his free time, he writes and records music, collects vintage computers, and enjoys nature. He lives in Raleigh, NC.

data.title: An "ice battery" system is being used to cool buildings and lower energy costs
data.author: addaon
data.article_summary: "Ice batteries" aim to reduce air conditioning costs by freezing water at night when electricity is cheaper. The system, installed in buildings like Manhattan's Eleven Madison, creates large amounts of ice that are used for cooling during the day, cutting cooling costs by up to 40%. This approach alleviates stress on the power grid during peak hours, especially in summer when air conditioning accounts for a significant portion of energy use. While currently used in around 4,000 sites globally, scientists are exploring materials that can store cool energy without needing to reach ice-cold temperatures, making the system adaptable to different climates. Despite potential, widespread home use is still in the future.

44188053.article_content:
"Ice batteries" aim to cut electric costs
"Ice batteries" aim to cut down on high electric costs of air conditioning
02:53
New York
— In the heart of Manhattan, four stories below ground, the iconic Eleven Madison skyscraper is being air-conditioned using ice.
"There's about 500,000 pounds of ice created every night," said Holly Paeper, president of Trane Technologies Commercial HVAC Americas business, the company responsible for installing the system it calls an ice battery. "And to put that into context, think about three city buses full of ice cubes."
The ice battery system freezes water at night when the cost of electricity is low. Then, during the day, when the price is high, the building is cooled with the previous night's ice instead of using
expensive electricity
. Trane
says
that this system can lower cooling costs by up to 40%.
"So, when everyone else is using their electricity in the middle of July to cool their building or to cool their homes, it's a big draw on the grid," Paeper said. "This building won't draw from that because it made its ice last night."
Air conditioning makes up about 20% of energy use in homes and businesses worldwide,
according to
a 2018 report from the International Energy Agency. But on the hottest days, it can account for more than 70% of electricity use during peak hours, per a
2023 IEA report
.
"We've done installations at about 4,000 sites globally," Paeper said. "There are six million commercial buildings in the U.S. alone, and a very small fraction of them have installations like this."
The problem that scientists like Dr. Patrick Shamberger are trying to solve isn't an overall lack of energy — it's when too many energy consumers are trying to use electricity at the same time, which puts stress on the grid.
"We don't want to build a whole bunch of excess power plants to just sit around, never turned on until that hot, hot day in August," said Shamberger, an associate professor of materials science and engineering at Texas A&M. "It's a lot of capital investment that doesn't get used."
So, instead of building more power plants, the focus is on storing energy with a system such as ice batteries. But because the process of freezing water uses a lot of energy itself, Shamberger and others are testing new materials that don't need to get as cold as ice, but can still keep buildings cool.
"We take water, we add some other elements and molecules to it," Shamberger explained. "And based on the composition, we can control that temperature basically anywhere we want it, in the zero to 20 C range. And that's important, because what might work great here in Texas, maybe it's not the right temperature to store your heat at if you're in Nevada, or in Wisconsin, say."
According to
an analysis released last month by the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, a Washington, D.C.-based energy advocacy group, home electricity bills in the U.S. this summer are expected to rise to an average of $784 for the summer period, from June through September, up 6.2% from last year's projected average of $737.
It marks
the highest such average in the 12 years that NEADA has been tracking summer residential cooling.
Shamberger said he sees a world where this system can be used to cool homes.
"Absolutely, yeah...but we're a little bit far out, right?" he said.

data.title: Merlin Bird ID
data.author: twitchard
data.article_summary:
Merlin是一个由eBird支持的鸟类识别应用，提供三种主要功能：  
1. **声音识别（Sound ID）**：实时听取并识别周围鸟鸣，支持离线使用，适用于美国、加拿大、欧洲及部分中南美和印度的鸟类。  
2. **照片识别（Photo ID）**：通过照片识别鸟类，也支持离线使用。  
3. **鸟类识别向导（Bird ID Wizard）**：通过回答三个简单问题，提供可能的鸟类匹配列表，适用于全球。  
此外，用户可以通过"Save My Bird"功能保存已识别的鸟类到个人列表，并使用eBird数据创建自定义鸟类观察列表。应用还提供专家建议和全球鸟类分布图，帮助用户更好地识别和了解鸟类。

Identify Bird Songs and Calls
Sound ID
listens to the birds around you and shows real-time suggestions for who’s singing. Compare your recording to the songs and calls in Merlin to confirm what you heard. Sound ID works completely offline, so you can identify birds you hear no matter where you are.
Available for birds in the US, Canada, Europe, with some common birds of Central and South America, and India. More species and regions coming soon.
More About Sound ID
Identify Birds in a Photo
Snap a photo of a bird, or pull one in from your camera roll, and
Photo ID
will offer a short list of possible matches. Photo ID works completely offline, so you can identify birds in the photos you take no matter where you are.
More about Photo ID
Bird ID Wizard—Step-by-step
Answer three simple questions about a bird you are trying to identify and Merlin will give you a list of possible matches. Merlin offers quick identification help for all levels of bird watchers and outdoor enthusiasts to help you learn about the birds in any country in the world.
Regions Merlin Covers
Save Birds to Your Life List
Build a digital scrapbook of your birding memories with Save My Bird. Tap “This is my bird!” each time you identify a bird, and Merlin will add it to your growing life list.
Save Your Birds with Merlin
Explore Lists of Birds Near You
Merlin is powered by
eBird
, allowing you to build custom lists of the birds you’re likely to spot wherever you are. Use the filter options to explore birds for different locations or time of year, or switch to show all the Offline Birds you’ve downloaded. Get more from the app with these
Merlin Tips and Tricks
.
See How Merlin Can Help You ID Birds
The Best Birding App, Powered By You
Merlin features the best of community contributed photos, songs, and calls, tips from experts around the world to help you ID the birds you see, and range maps from
Birds of the World
—all powered by billions of bird observations submitted to
eBird
.

data.title: The Art of SQL Query Optimization
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了SQL查询优化中的“计划探索器”工具，该工具帮助可视化和分析PostgreSQL查询优化器的决策过程。SQL是声明性语言，只指定查询结果，而数据库管理系统（DBMS）负责确定生成结果的最有效计划。查询优化器通过评估不同计划的成本来选择最优方案。然而，确定DBMS何时选择某方案或切换方案较为困难。

计划探索器工具通过在二维搜索空间上迭代，为每个参数组合生成SQL查询计划，并创建多种图表，展示计划变化、预期与实际返回的元组数量等。这些图表不仅具有艺术性，还提供了对优化器决策的深入理解，例如何时使用特定索引。

该工具最初是无需服务器的网页应用，使用WebAssembly版的PostgreSQL（PGlite）在浏览器中运行。最新版本增加了可选的服务器模式，通过REST接口将查询发送到实际的PostgreSQL服务器，以处理大数据集和自定义扩展。

工具生成的图表包括使用的查询计划、预期成本、实际执行时间、预期和实际结果元组数量等，帮助数据库管理员和开发者分析和优化查询计划。

44187777.article_content:
SQL is a declarative language; only the result of the query is specified. The exact steps to produce the result must be determined by the DBMS. Often, multiple ways exist to calculate a query result. For example, the DBMS can choose to use an index or perform a sequential scan on a table to find the needed tuples.
The query optimizer is responsible for finding the most efficient plan for a given query. The plan generator creates possible plans, which are then evaluated based on their costs. Afterward, the cheapest plan is chosen and executed. When the DBMS expects to return a large portion of the table, a full table scan can be more efficient than following the pointers in an index structure. However, it is hard to determine when the DBMS prefers one plan over another and when the switch between plans occurs.
In a few evenings of vibe coding,
I implemented the plan explorer
for PostgreSQL. It iterates over a search space and generates visualizations that show when the plan changes and how many tuples are expected versus the actual number returned. This blog post examines the “art” of query optimization. It discusses the plan explorer tool, the images the tool generates, and the insights the tool provides into the decisions made by the PostgreSQL query optimizer.
Plan Explorer
Plan Explorer is a tool that iterates over a two-dimensional search space and executes a given SQL query for each parameter combination. Based on the returned query plans (and actual query executions), various diagrams are generated. These diagrams have an artistic aspect, but they also provide valuable insights into the workings of the query optimizer and visually represent the decisions made (i.e., at which point PostgreSQL considers using a specific index).
The tool is based on the ideas of
Picasso
, but implemented as a modern web application.
The Picasso database query optimizer visualizer, Jayant R. Haritsa, Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment, Volume 3, Issue 1-2, September 2010
Server Mode
Initially, the tool was developed as a standalone website that does not require any server component. The WebAssembly build of PostgreSQL,
PGlite
, is used to run PostgreSQL within the user’s browser and extract the needed query plans.
In the most recent version of the tool, an optional server mode was added. Using this server mode, queries are sent to a
REST
endpoint on a web server. On the web server, a script can take the requested queries and forward them to an actual PostgreSQL server. The server component acts as a proxy for query execution. This is necessary because, due to security constraints, JavaScript running in a browser cannot open network connections to other hosts. So, to communicate with a real PostgreSQL server, the proxy component is needed. However, when an actual PostgreSQL server is queried, large datasets can be preloaded or custom extensions can be integrated into the database server. This allows the tool to run in these environments as well (e.g., a PostgreSQL extension developer could check their custom cost models and whether PostgreSQL picks up the desired query plans).
The architecture of the plan explorer is shown in the diagram below:
flowchart LR
subgraph **Browser**
UI["WebUI"]
PGLite["PGlite (WebAssembly PostgreSQL)"]
UI -- "SQL, Parameters" --> PGLite
PGLite -- "Query Results, Plans" --> UI
end
subgraph "**Proxy Mode** (Optional)"
Proxy["Proxy Server"]
PG["PostgreSQL Database"]
UI -- "HTTP (SQL/Params)" --> Proxy
Proxy -- "SQL" --> PG
PG -- "Results" --> Proxy
Proxy -- "Results" --> UI
end
A further feature of the server mode is that the queries can also be executed (
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)
) instead of only being planned (
EXPLAIN
). When only the planning of the query is performed, the tool operates much faster and can quickly iterate over the given search space. On the other hand, if the query is actually executed, PostgreSQL provides further information, such as the actual number of returned tuples or the execution time.
Generated Drawings
The plan explorer tool creates several different drawings from one query. These drawings are:
The used query plans
The expected costs of the query
The actual execution time of the query
The estimated number of result tuples
The actual number of result tuples
The difference between the estimated and actual number of result tuples
For a database administrator, the different query plans and their distribution might be the most interesting output of the tool. For a developer who has implemented custom scan nodes and cost models, the other outputs may also be of interest. They enable database developers to determine if the cost models function as expected.
Example Query Discussion

data
on the attribute
key
. Two predicates in the
WHERE
clause define filter conditions. The exact values for these conditions are determined by the search space. In this example, the

data.title: Air Lab – A portable and open air quality measuring device
data.author: 256dpi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：空气质量监测设备的选择与评价

不同观点：
• **支持AirGradient设备**：voxlax认为AirGradient设备价格更便宜、测量精度高，且硬件和软件都是开源的，可以自行刷机。他认为这对于关注准确性的人来说是一个不错的选择，并提供了自己使用该设备的体验链接。
• **强调产品诚实和设计**：hereme888赞赏AirGradient的网站设计简洁、产品真实，没有过度营销和复杂界面，认为这体现了产品背后的用心。
• **关注价格和可负担性**：homebrewer指出，对于生活在空气污染严重但经济条件有限的地区的人来说，200美元以上的设备过于昂贵，建议推出价格更低的基础版本。他强调，NO₂测量功能是该设备的一大亮点。
• **对Air Lab项目的反馈**：256dpi介绍了自己开发的Air Lab设备，该设备功能全面且开源，旨在让空气质量监测更易于定制和扩展。用户反馈中有人（如poisonborz）指出该设备的动画界面不实用，建议直接展示传感器数据。还有人（如ronakjain90）建议增加仅显示数据模式，以便用户自行选择展示方式。

补充讨论：
• **与其他产品的比较**：tigrezno认为Air Lab价格偏高，尤其是与具备空气净化功能的设备相比。neves询问是否有价格低于100美元的空气质量监测设备，特别是可以在AliExpress上购买的。
• **关于硬件选择的讨论**：部分用户对Air Lab的ESP32微控制器选择提出质疑，认为在功耗方面可能不如其他选择（如red523）。还有人关注设备是否支持Zigbee等集成系统（如xvfLJfx9）。
• **功能需求和改进建议**：一些用户提到对特定功能的需求，如PM2.5监测（savrajsingh）和Zigbee支持（xvfLJfx9）。此外，finnjohnsen2提到市场缺乏可用于自行组装的氡传感器模块。
• **开源社区和基础设施**：zevon提到sensor.community项目，该项目提供开源传感器设计和公共数据聚合基础设施。

争议焦点：
• **设备价格 vs. 功能性**：部分用户认为高价设备不具备空气净化功能，性价比不高。
• **界面设计 vs. 实用性**：一些用户认为Air Lab的动画界面不必要，更倾向于直接展示传感器数据。
• **可负担性 vs. 功能全面性**：价格较高的设备功能全面，但低收入地区用户更需要价格低廉的基础版本。

data.title: A Case for Feminism in Programming Language Design (2024)
data.author: smitty1e
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言（PL）设计中的性别视角和多样性，特别是女性在PL领域的体验和贡献。

不同观点：
• [andsoitis的观点] 作者以自身经历讲述了她对编程的热爱以及在编程语言领域中的成长，但同时也指出，PL研究和设计往往优先考虑机器而非人的需求。她认为当前的PL社区标准往往以男性化视角为主，注重形式化和技术评估，而忽视了用户研究和定性研究。她提出，通过引入女性主义视角，可以更好地审视PL的价值观和优先事项，并从多样化的视角改进编程语言设计。

• [MichealCodes的观点] 他引用了Grace Hopper的维基百科链接，暗示女性在编程历史中已有重要贡献，可能不需要特别强调性别视角，因为历史上已有女性做出了杰出贡献（如Grace Hopper）。

• [dismalaf的观点] 他认为作者不应仅仅批评现有编程语言缺乏女性视角，而应亲自去设计一种编程语言来证明自己的观点。

• [imgreen的观点] 他列举了多个由男性主导开发的编程语言，认为编程语言的设计历史上确实主要由男性主导，但质疑女性主义是否能真正推动PL设计的多样性和包容性。

• [iliti22的观点] 他讽刺地指出，女性可能更关注于衣服和TikTok舞蹈等活动，而不是像男性那样以编程为乐，暗示性别偏好可能影响了女性在编程领域的参与度。

• [tines的观点] 他认为某些PL设计者对错误信息的设计不够重视，而这种设计往往反映了设计者的生活经验和价值观。他特别提到，对于那些在编程世界中感到自己不属于该领域的人（如女性），不清晰的错误信息可能会带来负面影响。然而，tines也批评作者对成年用户的不尊重，认为不应该假设用户无法处理直接的错误信息。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于编程语言设计是否应该以及如何引入女性主义视角，特别是在错误信息设计和用户体验方面。一些人认为女性主义可以促进多样性和包容性，而另一些人则质疑其必要性或有效性。

• 对于如何在PL设计中体现多样性和包容性，有观点认为实际行动（如设计新的编程语言）比单纯批评现有设计更为有效。

• 对错误信息设计的讨论揭示了PL设计中一个具体而实际的改进方向，即更具可读性和用户友好的错误信息可能对所有用户都有帮助。

data.title: Binary Wordle
data.author: eh8
data.article_summary: 《Binary Wordle》是一款基于二进制数字（0和1）的猜词游戏，玩法类似于经典的Wordle。玩家通过键盘输入（0、1、Enter、Backspace）或使用按钮来参与游戏，目标是猜出正确的二进制序列。文章还包含了赞助商链接，推荐了一项名为altodial.com的电话服务，以及一个个人网站chengeric.com，提供更多有趣的内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于Wordle的二进制及数字变体游戏的玩法、难度和改进建议

不同观点：
• **对二进制版游戏的简单性提出质疑**：
  - [AmsterErdo] 认为二进制版游戏因为只有两个可能的值，因此很容易在两次尝试中猜中。
  - [umvi] 认为二进制确实简单，但十六进制版本更具挑战性，并分享了自己在编程游戏中的十六进制Wordle变体"dwordle"。
  - [abotsis] 也认为二进制版过于简单，建议改为“猜数字”的二进制形式，提供“太高”或“太低”的提示，并提议将猜测次数限制为5次以增加难度。

• **对游戏改进的建议**：
  - [NotAnOtter] 建议通过增加字符串长度和匹配子字符串的条件来提升游戏难度，使游戏更具挑战性。
  - [NoSalt] 和 [mulmen] 分享了自己的游戏结果，分别在两次和十次猜测中完成游戏，表明游戏对部分玩家来说可能过于简单。
  
• **其他数字变体游戏的分享**：
  - [zck] 分享了自己设计的多种基于Wordle的数字变体游戏，如"numberdle"、"rationerdle"、"factordle"和"formuladle"，并解释了每个变体的玩法和挑战性。
  - [James-Livesey] 提供了自己设计的十六进制版本链接，并提到之前的二进制版本因过于简单而不太受欢迎。

• **对游戏创意的赞赏与技术反馈**：
  - [Aissen] 赞赏游戏创意的趣味性，鼓励继续创新。
  - [bitwrangler] 对游戏的UI和动画表示赞赏，并指出游戏可以帮助学习二进制运算。
  - [thehours] 提供了技术反馈，指出输入时遇到的问题，无法用键盘输入除'0'以外的字符。

• **幽默和调侃**：
  - [tylerchr] 引用妻子的幽默评论，指出二进制版不应称为Wordle，而应叫"Digitle"。
  - [patrakov] 分享了一个简单的二步猜测策略，进一步强调了游戏的简单性。
  - [asimovDev] 提到另一个类似的游戏"Horsle"，引发对更多变体的联想。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于二进制版游戏的难度过低，玩家们提出了多种增加挑战性的建议。
- 玩家们分享了自己设计的各种Wordle变体游戏，展示了创造性和对游戏机制的深入理解。
- 技术反馈和幽默评论为讨论增添了趣味性和实用性。

data.title: DiffX – Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了传统Unified Diffs在现代软件开发中的局限性，并提出了一种新的可扩展差异格式——DiffX。Unified Diffs仅标准化了一部分差异信息，如文件标识、差异块偏移和增删行，但在编码、版本控制、元数据和文件路径表示等方面缺乏统一标准，导致解析和处理困难。文章指出，Unified Diffs无法表示提交列表、二进制补丁、文本编码，且缺乏标准的元数据格式。为解决这些问题，文章提出了DiffX格式，它完全向后兼容现有工具，具备未来适应性，且保持人类可读性。DiffX通过定义结构化和标准化格式，解决了Unified Diffs的不足，使得工具能更可靠地处理差异文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Diff格式的设计及其在不同工具中的应用和问题

不同观点：
• laserbeam认为当前的层次化格式（带有"..meta"和"…meta"）不易读，建议使用具有不同名称的结构以提高可读性，并质疑为何使用JSON和key=value两种格式。他还提到格式对分割diff的影响，以及对修订版本作为文件属性的困惑。
• HelloNurse指出提议中存在不必要的功能扩展，如单个diff表示多个提交列表和二进制补丁表示，认为这些功能过于复杂且不必要。
• blacklion批评当前格式混合了自定义头和JSON有效载荷，认为这种结构混乱且需要两个解析器，同时对扩展diff添加元数据的想法表示认可，但对其具体实现持批评态度。
• ed认为现有的patch格式已经解决了这些问题，并引用了git-format-patch文档作为支持。
• bawolff质疑是否真的需要这些新功能，认为多diff表示多个提交更自然，且元数据主要在单个系统内部有用。
• xyzzy_plugh认为文档难以阅读，指出diff和patch的区别，并质疑新格式是否真正解决了问题，建议如果元数据必须是JSON会更合理。
• redleader55质疑新格式试图解决的问题及其目标用户。
• itake提到diff工具对新行属性的依赖问题，认为长行变化的审查困难。
• tlb认为最通用和明确的diff表示方式是直接包含两个文件的内容，并指出diff格式在人类可读性上的不足。
• koiueo认为JSON不适合作为元数据的通用格式，过于复杂。
• greatgib不支持使用多行JSON或YAML，认为这会使格式变得复杂，并强调diff文件的单行命令特性。
• signa11推荐difftastic，认为其使用tree-sitter提供更好的diff信息。
• chipx86（DiffX作者之一）解释了DiffX的背景和目标，强调其解决工具在处理不同SCM系统的diff文件时遇到的问题，包括元数据、编码、二进制文件处理等，并指出新格式的必要性和设计决策。
• xiphias2认为新格式向后兼容但向前不兼容，建议通过文档化现有git diff源代码来解决问题，而非创建新格式。
• b0a04gl认为这是在过度工程化一个并不紧迫的问题，开发人员更需要不会因文件重命名或行结束符变化而崩溃的工具。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新格式的必要性和复杂性，一些人认为现有工具和格式已经足够，而另一些人则强调新格式在处理不同SCM系统的元数据和二进制文件方面的优势。
• 对JSON作为元数据格式的适用性存在分歧，一些人认为其过于复杂，而另一些人认为其通用性和易解析性是优势。
• 对新格式中引入的多层次结构和混合格式表示不满，认为这会增加解析和理解的难度。
• 实际使用中的问题，如长行变化的审查困难、文件重命名和行结束符变化带来的工具问题，也被提及并讨论。

44176737.article_content:
DiffX - Next-Generation Extensible Diff Format
¶
If you’re a software developer, you’ve probably worked with diff files. Git
diffs, Subversion diffs, CVS diffs.. Some kind of diff. You probably haven’t
given it a second thought, really. You make some changes, run a command, a
diff comes out. Maybe you hand it to someone, or apply it elsewhere, or put it
up for review.
Diff files show the differences between two text files, in the form of
inserted (
+
) and deleted (
-
) lines. Along with this, they contain some
basic information used to identify the file (usually just the name/relative
path within some part of the tree), maybe a timestamp or revision, and maybe
some other information.
Most people and tools work with
Unified Diffs
. They look like this:
--- readme    2016-01-26 16:29:12.000000000 -0800
+++ readme    2016-01-31 11:54:32.000000000 -0800
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
RCS file: /cvsroot/readme,v
retrieving version 1.1
retrieving version 1.2
diff -u -p -r1.1 -r1.2
--- readme    26 Jan 2016 16:29:12 -0000        1.1
+++ readme    31 Jan 2016 11:54:32 -0000        1.2
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or this:
diff --git a/readme b/readme
index d6613f5..5b50866 100644
--- a/readme
+++ b/readme
@@ -1 +1,3 @@
Hello there
+
+Oh hi!
Or even this:
Index: readme
===================================================================
--- (revision 123)
+++ (working copy)
Property changes on: .
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Modified: myproperty
## -1 +1 ##
-old value
+new value
Or this!
==== //depot/proj/logo.png#1 ==A== /src/proj/logo.png ====
Binary files /tmp/logo.png and /src/proj/logo.png differ
Here’s the problem
¶
Unified Diffs themselves are not a viable standard for modern development.
They only standardize parts of what we consider to be a diff, namely the
---
/
+++
lines for file identification,
@@
...
@@
lines for
diff hunk offsets/sizes, and
-
/
+
for inserted/deleted lines.
They
don’t
standardize encodings, revisions, metadata, or even how
filenames or paths are represented!
This makes it
very
hard for patch tools, code review tools, code analysis
tools, etc. to reliably parse any given diff and gather useful information,
other than the changed lines, particularly if they want to support multiple
types of source control systems. And there’s a lot of good stuff in diff files
that some tools, like code review tools or patchers, want.
You should see what GNU Patch has to deal with.
Unified Diffs have not kept up with where the world is going. For instance:
A single diff can’t represent a list of commits
There’s no standard way to represent binary patches
Diffs don’t know about text encodings (which is more of a problem than you
might think)
Diffs don’t have any standard format for arbitrary metadata, so everyone
implements it their own way.
We’re long past the point where diffs should be able to do all this. Tools
should be able to parse diffs in a standard way, and should be able to modify
them without worrying about breaking anything. It should be possible to load a
diff, any diff, using a Python module or Java package and pull information out
of it.
Unified Diffs aren’t going away, and they don’t need to. We just need to add
some extensibility to them. And that’s completely doable, today.
Here’s the good news
¶
Unified Diffs, by nature, are
very
forgiving, and they’re everywhere, in
one form or another. As you’ve seen from the examples above, tools shove all
kinds of data into them. Patchers basically skip anything they don’t
recognize. All they really lack is structure and standards.
Git’s diffs are the closest things we have to a standard diff format (in that
both Git and Mercurial support it, and Subversion pretends to, but poorly),
and the closest things we have to a modern diff format (as they optionally
support binary diffs and have a general concept of metadata, though it’s
largely Git-specific).
They’re a good start, though still not formally defined. Still, we can build
upon this, taking some of the best parts from Git diffs and from other
standards, and using the forgiving nature of Unified Diffs to define a new,
structured Unified Diff format.
DiffX files
¶
We propose a new format called Extensible Diffs, or DiffX files for short.
These are
fully backwards-compatible with existing tools
, while also being
future-proof
and remaining
human-readable
.
#diffx:
encoding=utf-8, version=1.0
#.change:
#..preamble:
indent=4, length=319, mimetype=text/markdown
Convert legacy header building code to Python 3.
Header building for messages used old Python 2.6-era list comprehensions
with tuples rather than modern dictionary comprehensions in order to build
a message list. This change modernizes that, and swaps out six for a
3-friendly `.items()` call.
#..meta:
format=json, length=270
{
"author"
:
"Christian Hammond <christian@example.com>"
,
"committer"
:
"Christi

data.title: An Arrow Flight SQL Server with DuckDB or SQLite back-end execution engines
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary:
GizmoSQL 是由 GizmoData™ 开发的 Apache Arrow Flight SQL 服务器实现，支持 DuckDB 或 SQLite 作为后端数据库。它支持通过中间件进行身份验证，并允许通过 TLS 进行加密连接。该项目最初是从 Voltron Data 的开源项目 sqlflite 分支而来，并在 Apache 2.0 许可证下独立扩展为 GizmoSQL。

用户可以通过发布的 Docker 镜像运行 GizmoSQL，并可选择启用或禁用 TLS。运行时可以挂载自定义的 DuckDB 数据库文件，该文件需使用 DuckDB 1.3.0 版本创建。此外，用户可在容器启动时执行初始化 SQL 命令，但选择查询结果不会显示，且失败的命令将导致服务器退出。最后，GizmoSQL 支持通过 JDBC 连接到服务器。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

Description
This is the GizmoSQL core repo - used to build an Apache Arrow Flight SQL server implementation using DuckDB or SQLite as a backend database.
It enables authentication via middleware and allows for encrypted connections to the database via TLS.
For more information about Apache Arrow Flight SQL - please see this
article
.
It is originally
forked from
sqlflite
, an open-source project developed by Voltron Data. I contributed to
sqlflite
while employed at Voltron Data, and have since independently extended and evolved the project into GizmoSQL under the Apache 2.0 License.
Option 1 - Running from the published Docker image
Open a terminal, then pull and run the published Docker image which has everything setup (change: "--detach" to "--interactive" if you wish to see the stdout on your screen) - with command:
#
Pull and run the Docker image
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--env PRINT_QUERIES=
"
1
"
\
--pull missing \
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
The above command will automatically mount a very small TPC-H DuckDB database file.
Note
: You can disable TLS in the container by setting environment variable:
TLS_ENABLED
to "0" (default is "1" - enabled).  This is not recommended unless you are using an mTLS sidecar in Kubernetes or something similar, as it will be insecure.
Optional - open a different database file
When running the Docker image - you can have it run your own DuckDB database file (the database must be built with DuckDB version: 1.3.0).
Prerequisite: DuckDB CLI
Install DuckDB CLI version
1.3.0
- and make sure the executable is on your PATH.
Platform Downloads:
Linux x86-64
Linux arm64 (aarch64)
MacOS Universal
In this example, we'll generate a new TPC-H Scale Factor 1 (1GB) database file, and then run the docker image to mount it:
#
Generate a TPC-H database in the host's /tmp directory
pushd
/tmp
duckdb ./tpch_sf1.duckdb
<<
EOF
.bail on
.echo on
SELECT VERSION();
INSTALL tpch;
LOAD tpch;
CALL dbgen(sf=1);
EOF
#
Run the gizmosql docker container image - and mount the host's DuckDB database file created above inside the container
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--pull missing \
--mount type=bind,source=
$(
pwd
)
,target=/opt/gizmosql/data \
--env DATABASE_FILENAME=
"
data/tpch_sf1.duckdb
"
\
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
Running initialization SQL commands
You can now run initialization commands upon container startup by setting environment variable:
INIT_SQL_COMMANDS
to a string of SQL commands separated by semicolons - example value:
SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';
.
Here is a full example of running the Docker image with initialization SQL commands:
#
Pull and run the Docker image
docker run --name gizmosql \
--detach \
--rm \
--tty \
--init \
--publish 31337:31337 \
--env TLS_ENABLED=
"
1
"
\
--env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD=
"
gizmosql_password
"
\
--env PRINT_QUERIES=
"
1
"
\
--env INIT_SQL_COMMANDS=
"
SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';
"
\
--pull missing \
gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
You can also specify a file containing initialization SQL commands by setting environment variable:
INIT_SQL_COMMANDS_FILE
to the path of the file containing the SQL commands - example value:
/tmp/init.sql
.  The file must be mounted inside the container.
Note
: for the DuckDB back-end - the following init commands are automatically run for you:
SET autoinstall_known_extensions = true; SET autoload_known_extensions = true;
Note
: Initialization SQL commands which SELECT data will NOT show the results (this is not supported).
Note
: Initialization SQL commands which fail will cause the Flight SQL server to abort and exit with a non-zero exit code.

Downlo

data.article_summary: "3D Model Playground" 是一个开源网页应用，允许用户通过手势和语音命令实时控制3D模型。该项目使用 Three.js 进行3D渲染，MediaPipe 进行手势追踪，Web Speech API 进行语音识别。用户可以通过说 "drag"（拖拽）、"rotate"（旋转）、"scale"（缩放）或 "animate"（动画）来改变互动模式，并通过捏合手指控制3D模型。此外，用户还可以拖放 GLTF 格式的3D模型到页面进行导入。该项目需要现代浏览器支持 WebGL，并访问摄像头和麦克风。项目代码可在 GitHub 获取，并遵循 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对新展示的技术或产品的反馈及建议

不同观点：
• [corysama] 指出该技术在演示中需要将手放在腿上操作，否则用户可能会很快感到手臂疲劳（"gorilla arm" syndrome）。
• [getToTheChopin] 分享了一个视频 demo，以具体展示该技术的工作方式，但没有进一步评论或分析。
• [doakes] 表达了对该技术及其不同模式的喜爱，并提到了类似的产品 Leap Motion，表现出对这类技术的长期兴趣。
• [chimpansteve] 提到了Leap Motion这个已有的类似产品，并询问当前是否还有支持，显示出对旧技术现状的关注。
• [ugh123] 提出了具体的功能建议，例如使用特定的手指姿势来触发旋转和缩放功能，以增强用户交互体验。
• [danvoell] 对该技术表示赞赏，认为它为实体游戏开辟了新世界，尤其看好其在游戏领域的潜力。
• [xnx] 表示对屏幕上的操作说明感到困惑，建议增加图像或动画来更好地解释控制方式，强调了用户界面设计的重要性。
• [ednite] 对该技术表示高度认可，认为它对互动内容创作和产品展示非常有用，并表示会进一步测试，显示出对实际应用的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户如 [doakes] 和 [chimpansteve] 提到了 Leap Motion 这一类似技术，显示出对新技术与旧技术之间比较的潜在兴趣。
• [corysama] 和 [xnx] 提出了对用户体验方面的担忧和建议，强调了技术演示中用户舒适度和界面清晰性的重要性。
• [ugh123] 提供了具体的功能增强建议，反映出用户对该技术未来发展的期望和创意贡献。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在用户体验的细节上，例如操作疲劳和界面说明不清楚等问题，但这些并非直接冲突，而是对技术改进的建议。

data.title: Track Errors First
data.author: GarethX
data.article_summary: 文章强调了在构建可观察性系统时，应首先关注错误（errors），因为错误是系统出现问题时最直接、最有价值的信号。作者指出，尽管传统的可观察性模型包括日志、指标和追踪三个支柱，但它们无法直接指出代码出错的具体位置。相比之下，错误提供了明确的堆栈轨迹、本地变量、请求数据和用户上下文等关键信息。文章建议，在系统出错时应尽可能多地收集上下文信息，而不是仅仅收集分散的日志或指标数据。此外，作者提醒开发者，虽然许多应用性能监控（APM）工具声称跟踪错误，但往往仅限于计数或简单汇总，未能提供完整的错误细节。作者强调，错误应被视为首要关注点，而非次要的数据点。文章最后提到，作者是错误跟踪工具Bugsink的创始人，并基于这一理念构建了该工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：程序开发中的错误处理与日志记录方法，以及不同工具和平台（如Sentry、Bugsink等）的使用体验和评价。

不同观点：
• [arnsholt] 认为在开发过程中应该大量抛出错误，以提醒开发者注意未保持的不变量。在生产环境中，错误越接近源头处理越容易，避免错误状态被持久化后引发更复杂的问题。
• [edelbitter] 强调错误不仅仅是另一个事件，它带有特定的上下文。所有的日志事件都应该带有上下文，以便更容易追踪问题。对随机出现的警告日志感到困扰，因为它们缺乏必要的上下文信息。
• [marcosdumay] 指出可观察性社区中日志充满了无用信息，导致错误信息容易被淹没，认为这是该社区发展过程中必然的结果，但已经到了可以忽视这些信息的阶段。
• [jensenbox] 喜欢使用Sentry，但认为它变得过于复杂，欢迎市场上有更多竞争者出现。
• [bheesink] 测试了Bugsink，并对其在Django项目中的表现感到满意，尤其看重其数据隐私保护特性，确保数据留在欧盟境内。
• [rco8786] 依赖Sentry进行错误跟踪，乐见市场上有新的竞争产品出现。
• [arp242] 认为日志在生产问题调试中很少有用，而错误信息则几乎总是有帮助。批评了许多组织在日志中产生大量“噪音”，使得错误信息被忽略。
• [jtwaleson] 期待有一个自托管的Sentry替代方案，因为数据过滤总是滞后，容易泄露用户隐私。

补充讨论：
• [MattSayar] 提出MELT（Metrics, Errors, Logs, Traces）的概念，认为这些元素都是有用的。
• [18172828286177] 回应MELT，认为良好的日志能够指出代码出错的位置。
• [827a] 询问当前大家使用的错误报告工具。
• [bugsense] 简单提到“传递火炬”，暗示可能是在告别或转型。

争议焦点：
• 错误与日志在开发和生产环境中的作用与重要性。部分开发者认为日志信息缺乏上下文，难以追踪问题，而错误信息则更加直接和有用。
• Sentry等工具的复杂性与隐私保护问题，部分开发者欢迎更多简单和自托管的替代方案。

44190643.article_content:
Track Errors First
Klaas van Schelven;
June 4 - 5 min read
Observability usually means collecting dashboards, traces, metrics, and logs — or at least, that’s how it’s sold.
What’s often missing from that conversation is
the most valuable signal
of all:
errors.
When an exception is raised, your code is telling you:
this was not supposed to happen
. Not just that something is
slow, or that usage is spiking — but that
your assumptions, as a programmer, just failed
.
That makes an exception — a real, raised error — the single most useful event you can track.
If you’re building out observability, whether for the first time or revisiting an existing setup,
start with that
.
The three pillars of observability
The standard model splits observability into three pillars:
logs, metrics, and traces
. They’re helpful, but something
is missing — and if you only follow this model, you’ll miss it too.
Logs
tell you what the system thought was worth noting.
Metrics
show trends over time: request duration, error rates, cache hit ratios.
Traces
give a sense of flow: what did this request call, and how long did it take?
All of those are useful. But none of them tell you
where the code broke
. For that, you need proper error tracking.
Signal Over Noise
There’s nothing more direct than a thrown exception. You don’t have to guess whether it’s important.
It’s the system saying:
this should not have happened, and here’s the line where it went wrong.
Right to the heart of the problem: a stacktrace with local variables
And because exceptions are so rare – so high-signal – it’s worth going deep when they happen. You want to capture:
The full stacktrace
— readable, with line numbers and source references
Local variables
— so you know what was actually passed in
Request data
— like URL paths, headers, or session info
User context
— who was affected, what were they doing?
You can’t get this from a metric. And you usually don’t get it from a log line unless you’ve done a
lot of extra
work
.
So instead of collecting a little information about everything that works — one trace here, one log line there — you’re
better off collecting
as much context as possible
at the moment your system breaks.
As one developer put it:
“One exception is worth a thousand logs.”
Missing from the Diagram
The canonical “three pillars” of observability are logs, metrics, and traces.
But
error tracking isn’t even mentioned
.
If you believe exceptions are your highest-signal events — and you probably should — then this model doesn’t just feel
incomplete.
It’s actively misleading.
It reflects what’s easy to generalize, easy to collect, and easy to sell — not necessarily what’s most useful when your
code breaks.
The Temple of Observability, with Errors fallen to the side
Technically Covered
In most observability platforms, errors are not missing — just abstracted.
They show up in logs, get counted in metrics, or appear as failed spans in traces. Some platforms file them under
generic “events,” alongside cache misses, deployments, and GC pauses.
This flattening makes implementation easier. Everything becomes a stream of telemetry — uniform, processable, and easy
to route.
But that abstraction comes at a cost. An exception isn’t just another event.  It’s your code
telling you it failed
,
in a specific place, with a specific context. If the system treats that like just another row in a data pipeline, you’ll
likely get the minimum: a message string, maybe a timestamp, maybe a partial trace.
Error tracking requires collecting more.
Stack traces, local variables, request metadata, user context — details
that rarely make it into standard logs or metric counters.
So yes, errors are technically covered. But they’re not treated as meaningful failures. Just another data point, in a
sea of unrelated ones.
You’re (probably) not Google
You’re probably not Google. And even if you are,
errors should come first — APM second.
Exceptions give you the clearest, most actionable signal when something breaks. You want full context, not a red dot on a
dashboard.
Plenty of APM tools claim to track errors — but often that just means counting them.
You get a spike on a chart, maybe a summary, rarely the full story. If exceptions are your highest-signal events, that
shouldn’t be an afterthought.
And watch out even with dedicated error tracking tools. Some of them started strong, fast, focused, developer-first,
but have since drifted into full observability platforms. Dashboards got added, then tracing, then metrics pipelines.
More tabs, more noise, more clicks.
So take a moment to check: Are errors still first-class in your stack? Or just another checkbox on a sales sheet?
Not your Neutral Observer
So who’s your friendly author? I’m Klaas,
the founder of
Bugsink
: an error tracking tool.
So yes, I have a stake in this – but not by accident.
I built a tool around this belief, not the other way around. And I think the current ecosystem, with its emphasis on
full-stack APM suites and dashboard-driv

data.title: Canadian Government Buries “Lawful Access” Provisions in New Border Bill
data.author: tunapizza
data.article_summary: 《Privacy At Risk: Government Buries Lawful Access Provisions in New Border Bill》一文指出，加拿大政府在《强边境法》(Bill C-2)中暗藏了允许无证访问互联网用户信息的条款。这些条款涉及无证访问互联网用户数据、制定新的全球生产命令以及加强对电子服务提供商数据的访问，旨在扩大执法部门的权限。自1999年以来，加拿大执法机构一直试图通过各种法案获取互联网用户数据，但多次因公众和法院的反对而失败。2014年，最高法院在Spencer案中裁定用户信息受隐私保护。尽管如此，执法部门仍试图通过将无证访问与边境安全等问题挂钩来推动立法。文章批评了这种将无关网络数据访问条款纳入边境安全法案的过度行为。

不同观点：
• **redm的观点**：认为政客经常通过在不同时间以略微不同的语言重复提交类似的法律条款，直到这些条款最终通过。这种做法被视为一种不正当的“法律闹剧”，且往往会成功。这种评论反映了对于立法过程中的漏洞和政客操纵手法的批评。

• **transcriptase的观点**：指出了加拿大司法系统中存在的一些问题，包括找到和起诉犯罪分子后，由于保释制度和法院积压案件，犯罪分子可能会很快被释放或者案件被撤销。具体提到加拿大最高法院对审理时间的严格限制，导致案件可能因为无法及时审理而被撤销，或者因为辩护律师提出的系统性问题作为辩护理由而被释放。这一观点反映了对于刑事司法系统效率和公平性的质疑。

• **dismalaf的观点**：批评了加拿大的选民和政客，特别是对前加拿大央行行长卡尼（Carney）的转变表示不满。评论认为卡尼在竞选时表现得像一个保护国家和民族主义的角色，但当选后却回归到全球主义和权威主义的立场。这个评论反映了对政客言行不一以及选民判断能力的质疑。

• **争议焦点**：不同评论对加拿大法律和政治体系的有效性和公正性存在争议。例如，redm和transcriptase对立法和司法过程中的漏洞和不公提出批评，而petermcneeley则引用了政府为应对特定问题所采取的措施。dismalaf的评论则更多地关注政客的言行不一和选民的判断能力。

44190832.article_content:
Welcome Mat by Bruce Bortin https://flic.kr/p/dZGkk CC BY-NC 2.0
News
Privacy At Risk: Government Buries Lawful Access Provisions in New Border Bill
June 4, 2025
The government yesterday introduced the
Strong Border Act (Bill C-2)
, legislation that was
promoted
as establishing new border measure provisions presumably designed to address U.S. concerns regarding the border. Yet buried toward the end of the bill are lawful access provisions that have nothing to do with the border. Those provisions, which raise the prospect of warrantless access to information about Internet subscribers, establish new global production orders of subscriber information, and envision new levels of access to data held by electronic service providers, mark the latest attempt in a longstanding campaign by Canadian law enforcement for lawful access legislation. Stymied by the Supreme Court of Canada (which has ruled that there is a
reasonable expectation of privacy in subscriber data
) and by repeated failures to present a compelling evidentiary case for warrantless access, law enforcement has instead tried to frame lawful access as essential to address everything from
organized crime
to
cyber-bullying
to (now)
border safety
. Much like the government’s overreach last year on online harms, Bill C-2 overreaches by including measures on Internet subscriber data that have nothing to do with border safety or security but raise privacy and civil liberties concerns that are bound to spark opposition. This post provides the background on lawful access and an overview of some Bill C-2’s provisions with more details on key elements to come.
Lawful Access Background
The pressure from Canadian law enforcement for access to Internet subscriber data dates back to 1999, when government officials began crafting proposals that included legal powers to access surveillance and subscriber information. What followed were a series of lawful access bills that sparked opposition – both in the public and effectively in the courts. For example, a 2010 lawful access bill included mandated the disclosure of Internet provider customer information, including customer name, address, phone number, email address, Internet protocol address, and a series of device identification numbers without court oversight.
That bill stalled, but in February 2012, then-Public Safety Minister Vic Toews introduced Internet surveillance legislation that once again sparked widespread criticism from across the political spectrum. Toews
infamously
said to Francis Scarpaleggia, now the Speaker of the House but then a critic of the bill, that he “could stand with us or with the child pornographers.” The comment did not help his case and the overwhelming negative publicity pressured the government to quickly backtrack by placing it on hold.
In 2013, then-Justice Minister Rob Nicholson announced that the bill was dead,
confirming
“we will not be proceeding with Bill C-30 and any attempts that we will continue to have to modernize the Criminal Code will not contain the measures contained in C-30.” Nicholson’s commitment lasted less than a year. By 2014, Peter MacKay, then the new federal justice minister, unveiled Bill C-13, which was marketed as an effort to crack down on cyber-bullying. Yet the vast majority of the bill brought back many (though not all) lawful access provisions found in the earlier proposal.
The lawful access campaign was effectively derailed for a decade by the Supreme Court of Canada. In the 2
014 Spencer decision
, the Court ruled that there was a reasonable expectation of privacy in Internet subscriber information:
in the totality of the circumstances of this case, there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in the subscriber information. The disclosure of this information will often amount to the identification of a user with intimate or sensitive activities being carried out online, usually on the understanding that these activities would be anonymous. A request by a police officer that an ISP voluntarily disclose such information amounts to a search.
There were some efforts to revive lawful access, but in 2017 the House of Commons Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security r
ecommended against introducing reforms
:
That at this time, and following the Supreme Court of Canada’s decision in R. v. Spencer, no changes to the lawful access regime for subscriber information and encrypted information be made, but that the House of Commons Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security continue to study such rapidly evolving technological issues related to cyber security.
Last year, the Supreme Court expanded the privacy safeguards in the
Bykovets decision
, ruling that “if section 8 of the Charter is to meaningfully protect the online privacy of Canadians in today’s overwhelmingly digital world, it must protect their IP addresses. An IP address is the crucial link between an Internet user and their online activity.” The case is discussed in th
